definition_zh: 排水；排水系统；排出的水；流域；引流
definition_en: the system or process by which water is removed from land, soil or a wound
core_image: 一片积水的田里，几条暗沟把水引向低处的河，水面一寸寸退下去
scene: 暴雨过后，低洼的农田积起半尺深的水，田垄间几条暗沟正把浑水引向旁边的河。Faulty drainage left the lower fields under water for a week.
sceneCN: 这里 drainage 指「排水系统、排水设施」（第 1 个义项：把地表或土壤中的水引走的沟渠与管网）；句意为排水系统出了故障，低处的田地积水达一周之久。

pos.zh: 排水；排水系统；排出的水；（医学）引流（不可数；指多套系统时作可数）

derivatives.zh: drain（本词的动词基础，零派生；古英语 dreahnian「沥干」）→ 排水；排干；耗尽
drain（由动词转类为零派生名词，无后缀）→ 下水道；排水管；消耗
drain + -er（古英语 -ere，施事后缀，与拉丁 -arius 同功能）→ 执行排水的器具：滤水器、沥水架
drain + -ed（古英语过去分词后缀）→ 已被排干的；引申为被掏空、精疲力竭
drain + -ing（古英语动名词与现在分词后缀）→ 排水的动作；引申为耗人的

senses.title: The system that carries water away
senses.titleCN: 排水系统：把水引走的整套设施
senses.definition: the network of ditches, pipes and channels that removes water from an area
senses.definitionCN: 把水从某地引走的沟渠、管道与渠道系统
senses.example: Faulty drainage left the lower fields under water for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 排水系统出了故障，低处的田地积水达一周之久。
senses.why: drainage is drain plus -age, and -age names a process or the whole apparatus that carries it out; the village owns not one ditch but a connected set of them.
senses.whyCN: drainage 是 drain 加 -age，而 -age 表示过程或执行该过程的整套装置；村子拥有的不是一条沟，而是一组相连的沟渠。

senses.title: The act of draining water off
senses.titleCN: 排水过程：把水排走这件事
senses.definition: the process of removing surplus water from soil, land or a structure
senses.definitionCN: 把多余的水从土壤、土地或建筑物中排走的过程
senses.example: Good drainage keeps the clay soil workable after heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 排水良好能让黏土在暴雨后仍然可耕。
senses.why: the same suffix names the action itself, so the word can refer to what is done rather than to the works that do it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也命名动作本身，因此这个词可以指「排水这件事」，而不是干这件事的设施。

senses.title: Water that has been drained away
senses.titleCN: 排出的水：被引走的液体
senses.definition: the water, often waste water, that is carried off by drains
senses.definitionCN: 被排水设施引走的水，常指污水
senses.example: The drainage from the mine carried heavy metals into the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 矿井排出的水把重金属带进了小溪。
senses.why: by metonymy the container word comes to name its contents: what the drains carry is also called drainage.
senses.whyCN: 通过转喻，容器之名转而指其中的内容：排水设施所输送的水也被叫作 drainage。

senses.title: The land area that sends water to a river
senses.titleCN: 流域：把水汇给某条河的地面
senses.definition: the whole area whose surface water flows into a particular river or basin
senses.definitionCN: 地表水全部流入某条河或某个盆地的整个区域
senses.example: The drainage of the upper valley feeds three reservoirs.
senses.exampleCN: 上谷的集水区供养着三座水库。
senses.why: hydrologists speak of what a river drains, so drainage shifts from the channel to the land that supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 水文学家谈「一条河排走哪片地面的水」，于是 drainage 从河道转到供养它的土地。

senses.title: How readily soil lets water through
senses.titleCN: 土壤排水性：水通过的快慢
senses.definition: the rate at which water moves down through soil or rock
senses.definitionCN: 水在土壤或岩层中向下移动的速率
senses.example: Heavy clay has poor drainage and stays wet for days.
senses.exampleCN: 重黏土的排水性差，会连续几天保持潮湿。
senses.why: a soil is judged by how fast it drains, so the abstract noun names a property of the ground rather than a structure.
senses.whyCN: 人们用「水排得多快」来评价土壤，因此这个抽象名词指的是地面的一种性质，而非某种结构。

senses.title: Medical drainage of a wound
senses.titleCN: 医学引流：把伤口液体引走
senses.definition: the removal of fluid from a wound or body cavity, or the fluid so removed
senses.definitionCN: 把液体从伤口或体腔引出，或指这样引出的液体
senses.example: The nurse checked the drainage from the wound each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每天早上检查伤口的引流液。
senses.why: medicine applies the same image to the body: fluid is given a path out, and the word names both the procedure and its product.
senses.whyCN: 医学把同一意象用到身体上：给液体一条出路，这个词既指操作也指引出的东西。

senses.title: Pumping water out of a mine or tunnel
senses.titleCN: 矿井与工程排水
senses.definition: the removal of ground water from a mine, tunnel or construction pit
senses.definitionCN: 从矿井、隧道或施工基坑中抽走地下水
senses.example: Mine drainage must be pumped out before the shaft can be deepened.
senses.exampleCN: 在加深竖井之前，必须先把矿井积水抽走。
senses.why: the engineering sense narrows the general idea to water that must be lifted out of a hole, because gravity will not do the work.
senses.whyCN: 工程义把一般概念收窄为「必须从坑里提上来的水」，因为重力无法把它带走。

senses.title: A steady loss of people or resources
senses.titleCN: 资源与人力的持续外流
senses.definition: a continuing loss of people, money or resources from a place or system
senses.definitionCN: 人、资金或资源从一个地方或系统中持续流失
senses.example: The drainage of trained nurses to big cities weakened the rural clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 受训护士流向大城市，削弱了乡村诊所。
senses.why: the metaphor treats a community as ground that loses its water through channels, leaving it dry.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把社区当作会沿沟渠失水的地面，水流走之后只剩干涸。

intro.en: Drainage is the native verb drain plus the noun suffix -age. Drain goes back to Old English dreahnian 'to strain out, draw off liquid', and -age reached English through Old French from Latin -aticum. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: drainage 是英语本族动词 drain 加名词后缀 -age 构成。drain 上承古英语 dreahnian「沥出、滤干液体」；-age 经古法语来自拉丁 -aticum。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dreahnian meant to strain or draw off liquid, and was used of a wound, a vessel or wet ground. The modern verb drain shortened both the vowel and the ending.
items.cn: dreahnian 意为沥出、引流液体，用于伤口、容器或潮湿地面。现代动词 drain 缩短了元音与词尾。

items.en: By the fourteenth century drainen is recorded for emptying a pond or a ditch. The noun drain, meaning a channel, appears later, in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪，drainen 已用于排空池塘或沟渠。表示通道的名词 drain 出现较晚，在 16 世纪。

items.en: The suffix -age entered English with Old French, from Latin -aticum, which formed nouns of action or collective status; attached to a verb it names the process or the set of works.
items.cn: 后缀 -age 随古法语进入英语，源自拉丁 -aticum，用来构成动作或集合状态的名词；接在动词后即命名过程或整套设施。

items.en: The noun drainage is recorded in the seventeenth century in writing on fen reclamation and water meadow management.
items.cn: 名词 drainage 在 17 世纪见于沼泽开垦与草甸灌溉管理的文献。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word covers urban sewerage, mine dewatering and the drainage basin as a unit of land.
items.cn: 19 世纪，这个词覆盖城市排污、矿井排水以及作为土地单元的流域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of drain is not settled; a link with Old English drygan 'to dry' is often proposed but not demonstrated, and the first dates above are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：drain 的更深来源没有定论；把它与古英语 drygan「使干」相联系的说法常被提出，但未获证实；上述首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds water-handling words that are constantly swapped; group two holds the terms for the land area that feeds a river.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换的水利词汇；第二组是命名「供养一条河的地面」的术语。

entries.definition: A single pipe or ditch that carries water away; drainage is the whole arrangement of such channels.
entries.definitionCN: 单条把水引走的管或沟；drainage 则是这类通道的整套安排。

entries.definition: An underground conduit built for sewage; drainage may also carry clean rain water.
entries.definitionCN: 专为污水建的地下管道；排水系统也可能输送干净的雨水。

entries.definition: Water that flows over the surface instead of entering the soil; drainage is what removes it.
entries.definitionCN: 未渗入土壤而在地表流走的水；排水系统负责把它引走。

entries.definition: Bringing water to land on purpose; drainage takes water away from it.
entries.definitionCN: 有意把水送到土地上；排水则把水从土地上带走。

entries.definition: The area from which rain and streams feed one river or reservoir.
entries.definitionCN: 雨水与小河汇入同一条河或同一水库的区域。

entries.definition: Either the dividing ridge between basins or, in North American usage, the basin itself.
entries.definitionCN: 既可指流域之间的分水岭，也可在北美用法中指流域本身。

entries.definition: A river, stream or artificial channel through which water flows.
entries.definitionCN: 水流经的河、溪或人工渠道。

entries.definition: The point or amount at which water leaves a lake, basin or system.
entries.definitionCN: 水离开湖泊、盆地或系统的出口或数量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real compounds and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、复合词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: drain + -age: the -age noun names what the verb does, as in seepage and leakage.
normal.cn: drain + -age：-age 名词命名动词所做的事，如 seepage、leakage。

normal.en: A drainage basin is not a basin you wash in: it is the land that drains into one river.
normal.cn: drainage basin 不是洗脸的盆，而是把水排入同一条河的土地。

normal.en: The word covers both the ditches and the water in them, as printing can mean the act and the product.
normal.cn: 这个词既指沟渠也指沟里的水，正如 printing 既可指印刷行为也可指印刷品。

normal.en: Medical drainage uses the same picture: fluid is shown a way out of the body.
normal.cn: 医学引流用同一幅画面：给液体一条离开身体的出路。

normal.en: Poor drainage is a soil property; blocked drainage is a broken system. The context tells you which reading is meant.
normal.cn: poor drainage 说的是土壤性质，blocked drainage 说的是系统堵塞；上下文决定读法。

abstract.en: A city without drainage is a city that keeps every storm it has ever met.
abstract.cn: 没有排水系统的城市，会把遇到过的每一场暴雨都留在原地。

abstract.en: When talented people leave a region, economists borrow the word and call it a drainage of talent.
abstract.cn: 人才离开某地时，经济学家借用这个词，称之为人才的流失。

abstract.en: A good conversation has drainage too: small channels that let pressure out before it floods.
abstract.cn: 好的对话也有排水：细小的通道让压力在泛滥之前先泄出去。

examples.en: The new drainage system carries rainwater away from the market.
examples.cn: 新的排水系统把雨水从市场引走。

examples.en: Poor drainage turns the path into mud after every storm.
examples.cn: 排水不良使小路每场暴雨后都变成泥浆。

examples.en: Engineers mapped the drainage of the whole valley before building the dam.
examples.cn: 工程师在筑坝前测绘了整个山谷的集水区。

dict_mnemonic.text: drain（排走）+ -age（过程、集合）＝把水引走的整套安排；沟渠、管网、流域都归到「水往哪里走」这一条线。

root: 由动词 drain（排走液体）加后缀 -age（过程、集合）构成；drain 上承古英语 dreahnian「沥出、滤干」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of drainage. The core is a path given to water: first the works, then the act, then the water itself, then the land that supplies it, and finally any steady outflow.
sensesIntro.cn: drainage 的八个义项。核心是「给水一条路」：先是设施，再是动作，再是被引走的水，再是供养它的土地，最后是任何持续的外流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water is given a path and led away from where it is not wanted.
core.cn: 核心意象：给水一条路，把它从不需要它的地方引走。

branches.en: WORKS AND ACT: the connected channels, then the process they perform.
branches.cn: 设施与动作：先是相连的通道，再是它们执行的过程。

branches.en: WHAT MOVES AND WHERE FROM: the water carried off, then the land that supplies it.
branches.cn: 流动之物与来源：先是被引走的水，再是供养它的土地。

branches.en: A PROPERTY OF GROUND: how fast soil lets water pass, with no pipe in sight.
branches.cn: 地面的性质：土壤让水通过得多快，此时并不需要管道。

branches.en: REMOVAL BY FORCE OR BY DESIGN: fluid drawn from a wound, water pumped from a mine.
branches.cn: 借力或设计而成的排出：从伤口引出液体，从矿井抽水。

branches.en: OUTFLOW AS LOSS: people and money leaving a place are treated as water leaving dry land.
branches.cn: 外流即流失：人与钱离开某地，被当作水离开干地。

intro.en: Drainage is drain plus -age. The suffix, not the root, is the borrowed element: -age turns the verb into the name of a process and of the apparatus that performs it.
intro.cn: drainage 由 drain 加 -age 构成。借来的是后缀而非词根：-age 把动词变成过程之名，也变成执行该过程的装置之名。

latinIntro.en: Drain itself is a Germanic word with no Latin cognate. Only the suffix is Latin in origin, coming through French from -aticum; Latin ripa and the drain family are unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: drain 本身是日耳曼语词，没有拉丁同族词。只有后缀源自拉丁，经法语来自 -aticum；拉丁 ripa 与 drain 词族无关。

items.example: The farmer drained the field before sowing.
items.exampleCN: 农夫在播种前把田里的水排干。

items.meaning: process, state or a collective set
items.example: Drainage, seepage and leakage all name processes.

items.meaning: a channel or pipe that carries liquid away
items.example: A drain runs along the edge of the road.

items.meaning: a device or person that drains
items.example: She lifted the drainer out of the sink.
items.exampleCN: 她把沥水架从水槽里拿起来。

items.example: He felt drained after the long shift.
items.exampleCN: 长时间值班后他感到精疲力竭。

items.meaning: the act of removing liquid; exhausting
items.example: Draining the pond took two days.

items.meaning: the land area drained by one river system
items.meaningCN: 由同一河系排水的陆地区域
items.example: The city lies inside the drainage basin of the Yangtze.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市位于长江流域之内。

items.meaning: a pipe that carries waste water away
items.example: A broken drainpipe flooded the basement.
items.exampleCN: 一根破损的排水管淹了地下室。

definition_zh: 支流；纳贡国；进贡者；支流的；纳贡的
definition_en: a stream that flows into a larger river, or a weaker state that pays tribute to a stronger one
core_image: 一条细流从山谷侧旁汇入大河，像把自家的水当作贡品交上去
scene: 山谷里一条清亮的小河从侧面汇入浑浊的大江，河口处两股水色分明。The clear tributary joins the muddy main river without mixing at first.
sceneCN: 这里 tributary 指「支流」（第 1 个义项：汇入更大河流的较小水道）；句意为清澈的支流汇入浑浊的干流，起初两股水并不混合。

pos.zh: 支流；纳贡国；进贡者（复数 tributaries）

forms.label: 形容词（同一形式作定语）

derivatives.zh: tribut-（拉丁 tributum「税、贡赋」）+ 零后缀 → 贡品；引申为颂词
con-（共同）+ tribut-（分配）+ -e（拉丁动词词尾）→ 把份额一起交出：贡献、捐助（同根，非本词直接派生）
contribute + -ion（拉丁 -io，表动作或结果）→ 贡献的行为或结果：捐款
dis-（分开）+ tribut-（分配）+ -e（拉丁动词词尾）→ 把份额分出去：分配、分发
distribute + -ion（拉丁 -io，表动作或结果）→ 分配的行为或结果：分布

senses.title: A stream that feeds a larger river
senses.titleCN: 支流：汇入更大河流的小水道
senses.definition: a smaller river or stream that flows into a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 汇入更大河流的较小河流或溪流
senses.example: The clear tributary joins the muddy main river without mixing at first.
senses.exampleCN: 清澈的支流汇入浑浊的干流，起初两股水并不混合。
senses.why: the tributary brings its water to a greater river as a subject brings tribute to a lord; the Latin word for a payer of tribute supplied the name.
senses.whyCN: 支流把水交给更大的河，正如属臣把贡品交给君主；命名正是来自拉丁语中「纳贡者」一词。

senses.title: One branch of a river system
senses.titleCN: 支流水系中的一支
senses.definition: a branch of a river system, viewed as one of its feeders
senses.definitionCN: 河系中的一条分支，被视为汇入干流的水道之一
senses.example: The map marks every tributary of the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 地图标出了三角洲的每一条支流。
senses.why: once the word names one stream, it extends to each branch in the network, so a system is described by its tributaries.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词命名一条水道，就扩展到网络中的每一条分支，于是整个水系用它的支流来描述。

senses.title: A state that pays tribute
senses.titleCN: 纳贡国：向强国交纳贡品的国家
senses.definition: a state that pays tribute to a stronger state in return for protection or toleration
senses.definitionCN: 为换取保护或容许而向更强国家纳贡的国家
senses.example: The small kingdom became a tributary of its powerful neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小王国成了强邻的纳贡国。
senses.why: the political sense is the oldest: a weaker state hands over goods as a stream hands over water.
senses.whyCN: 政治义最古老：弱国交出货物，正如小河交出水量。

senses.title: A ruler who pays tribute
senses.titleCN: 进贡者：交纳贡品的君主
senses.definition: a ruler or people that pays tribute to a superior power
senses.definitionCN: 向更强势力纳贡的君主或族群
senses.example: Tributary princes came to the capital each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 纳贡的诸侯每年春天来到都城。
senses.why: the noun can name the payer as well as the paying state, since both stand in the same subordinate relation.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既可指纳贡的国家，也可指纳贡者本人，因为二者处于同样的从属关系。

senses.title: Of a stream: joining a larger one
senses.titleCN: 形容词：支流的
senses.definition: of or forming a stream that flows into a larger river
senses.definitionCN: 属于或构成汇入更大河流的水道
senses.example: A tributary stream enters the lake from the north.
senses.exampleCN: 一条支流小溪从北面流入湖中。
senses.why: as an adjective the word simply modifies a stream, glacier or channel that joins a larger one.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词只是修饰汇入更大水体的溪流、冰川或水道。

senses.title: Of tribute: paid to a superior
senses.titleCN: 形容词：纳贡的
senses.definition: relating to tribute or to a state that pays it
senses.definitionCN: 与贡品有关的，或指交纳贡品的国家
senses.example: Tributary payments drained the kingdom's treasury.
senses.exampleCN: 纳贡支出耗尽了王国的国库。
senses.why: the adjective keeps the political sense and modifies payments, obligations or territories.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词保留政治义，用来修饰款项、义务或领地。

senses.title: A smaller source feeding a larger movement
senses.titleCN: 比喻：汇入主流的小支脉
senses.definition: a smaller source or group that adds to a larger movement or body
senses.definitionCN: 为更大运动或更大整体输送力量的小来源或小群体
senses.example: Regional journals are tributaries of the main scientific literature.
senses.exampleCN: 地方期刊是主流科学文献的支流。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the direction: something smaller flows into something larger and is absorbed by it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了方向：较小的东西流入较大的东西并被其吸收。

senses.title: Water and sediment contributed by a branch
senses.titleCN: 水文：支流对干流的水沙补给
senses.definition: the water and sediment that a branch contributes to the main river
senses.definitionCN: 一条分支向干流输送的水量与泥沙
senses.example: Tributaries supply most of the sediment that builds the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 建造三角洲的大部分泥沙由支流提供。
senses.why: hydrology measures what each tributary contributes, so the word can name the contribution itself.
senses.whyCN: 水文学测量每条支流贡献了多少，因此这个词也可命名所贡献的量。

intro.en: Tributary comes from Latin tributarius 'paying tribute', from tributum 'tax, tribute', from tribuere 'to allot, grant, pay', whose root is tribus 'a division of the Roman people'. The river sense is a modern metaphor. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tributary 来自拉丁 tributarius「纳贡的」，出 tributum「税、贡」，再出 tribuere「分配、给予」，根源为 tribus「罗马人民的部族划分」。河流义是近代比喻。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tribus named a division of the Roman people. Its own origin is uncertain: the ancient link with tri- 'three' is a tradition rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: tribus 指罗马人民的部族划分。其自身来源不确定：与 tri-「三」的古关联属传统说法，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: From tribus came tribuere 'to divide out, allot, grant, pay', a verb used for assigning shares and for paying what is owed.
items.cn: 由 tribus 得出 tribuere「分出、配给、给予、支付」，用于分配份额与偿付所欠。

items.en: Tributum was the tax or tribute levied on a subject people; the noun kept the sense of something handed over to a superior.
items.cn: tributum 是向属民征收的税或贡；这个名词保留了「交给上位者之物」的意思。

items.en: The adjective tributarius meant paying tribute, and English took it in the fourteenth century for princes and states in that relation.
items.cn: 形容词 tributarius 意为纳贡的；英语在 14 世纪用它指处于这种关系的君主与国家。

items.en: The stream sense appears in the nineteenth century, when geography described branches as paying their water to the main river; the metaphor is exact but the date is approximate.
items.cn: 河流义在 19 世纪出现，当时地理学把分支描述为向干流交纳水量；比喻很确切，但年代只是约数。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of tribus is disputed, and the first citation of the stream sense is not fixed. The political sense is the historically secure one.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代存疑）：tribus 的来源有争议，河流义的最早书证也未确定；政治义是历史上可靠的一支。

note.en: Group one holds words of the tribute family plus one false friend; group two holds ways of naming a stream that joins another.
note.cn: 第一组是 tribute 词族的词外加一个假朋友；第二组是命名「汇入另一水体的小水道」的其他说法。

entries.definition: Goods or money paid by one ruler or state to another as a sign of submission.
entries.definitionCN: 一方君主或国家向另一方交纳以表示臣服的财物。

entries.definition: An elected Roman official who protected the interests of the plebeians; the word is related through tribus.
entries.definitionCN: 古罗马保护平民利益的民选官员；该词经 tribus 与 tributary 同源。

entries.definition: A body or bench that hears and decides cases; it descends from the seat of a tribune.
entries.definitionCN: 审理并裁决案件的机构或法官席；源自保民官的席位。

entries.definition: Great suffering or trouble; it comes from Latin tribulare 'to thresh', not from tribute.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的苦难或磨难；来自拉丁 tribulare「打谷」，与 tribute 无关。

entries.definition: A division of a river, family or organization; a tributary is specifically one that flows into a larger river.
entries.definitionCN: 河流、家族或组织的分支；tributary 特指汇入更大河流的那一支。

entries.definition: A small stream that supplies a larger river or lake, stressing the supply rather than the hierarchy.
entries.definitionCN: 向更大河流或湖泊供水的小溪，强调补给而非等级关系。

entries.definition: The place where two rivers join; it names the junction, not the smaller stream.
entries.definitionCN: 两条河流汇合的地点；它命名汇合处，而非较小的那条河。

entries.definition: Water entering a lake or basin, or the rate at which it enters.
entries.definitionCN: 进入湖泊或盆地的水，或其进入的速率。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、同族词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: tributary = tribut- (tribute) + -ary: a stream that pays its water as tribute.
normal.cn: tributary = tribut-（贡品）+ -ary：把水当作贡品交上去的小河。

normal.en: The political sense is older; the river sense borrows the relation, not the goods.
normal.cn: 政治义更古老；河流义借的是这层关系，而不是货物。

normal.en: tributary, tribute, contribute and distribute all go back to tribuere 'to allot'.
normal.cn: tributary、tribute、contribute、distribute 都可追到 tribuere「分配」。

normal.en: A tributary is always smaller than what it joins; two equal rivers meet at a confluence.
normal.cn: 支流总比它汇入的水体小；两条同等的河相遇处叫汇流点。

normal.en: The adjective is mostly attributive: a tributary stream, a tributary state, rarely a predicative use.
normal.cn: 这个形容词多作定语：a tributary stream、a tributary state，很少作表语。

abstract.en: Every big movement has tributaries: small journals, local scenes and minor languages feeding a larger current.
abstract.cn: 每一种大潮流都有支流：小期刊、地方场景与少数语言为更大的水流补给。

abstract.en: A person's education is a tributary of the main stream of their life, adding water without becoming it.
abstract.cn: 一个人的教育是人生主河道的一条支流，添了水却没有变成主河道。

abstract.en: A rumour is a tributary of fear, small and steady, and it can raise the whole river.
abstract.cn: 谣言是恐惧的支流，细小而持续，却能把整条河抬高。

examples.en: The Missouri is a tributary of the Mississippi.
examples.cn: 密苏里河是密西西比河的一条支流。

examples.en: Several tributaries cut deep valleys into the plateau.
examples.cn: 几条支流在高原上切出深谷。

examples.en: The empire demanded annual tribute from its tributary states.
examples.cn: 帝国每年向纳贡国索取贡品。

dict_mnemonic.text: tributary = tribut（纳贡）+ -ary（与……有关）：一条小河把水当作贡品交给大河；罗马的属国、地图上的分支都用同一幅画面。

root: 源自拉丁 tributarius「纳贡的」，出 tributum「贡税」，再出 tribuere「分配、给予」，根源为 tribus「部族」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of tributary. The physical sense and the political sense are the same relation at two scales: a smaller unit hands over what it has to a larger one.
sensesIntro.cn: tributary 的八个义项。自然义与政治义是同一关系在两个尺度上的体现：较小的一方把自己所有的交给较大的一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small channel runs beside a great river and then gives it all its water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条小水道沿大河旁边流，最后把全部水量交给它。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL STREAM: the feeder itself, then the same word used as an adjective.
branches.cn: 自然水道：先是支流本身，再是同形形容词的用法。

branches.en: NETWORK AND CONTRIBUTION: each branch in the system, then the water and sediment it delivers.
branches.cn: 网络与贡献：系统中的每条分支，再是它输送的水与泥沙。

branches.en: THE POLITICAL RELATION: the subordinate state, then the ruler who pays.
branches.cn: 政治关系：先是属国，再是纳贡的君主。

branches.en: THE ADJECTIVE OF TRIBUTE: payments and obligations, with no river present.
branches.cn: 贡赋的形容词用法：款项与义务，此时没有河流。

branches.en: METAPHOR OF FEEDING: any small source that adds to a larger movement.
branches.cn: 补给隐喻：任何为更大运动添力的小来源。

intro.en: Tributary divides as tribut- plus -ary. The stem is the participle of Latin tribuere 'to allot'; -ary marks relation, so the word means 'relating to tribute'.
intro.cn: tributary 可切分为 tribut- 加 -ary。词干是拉丁 tribuere「分配」的分词形式；-ary 标记关系，因此整个词意为「与贡赋有关的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribuere yields a large English family: tribute, tributary, contribute, contribution, distribute, distribution and attribution. They share the idea of assigning a share.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tribuere 衍生出庞大的英语词族：tribute、tributary、contribute、contribution、distribute、distribution、attribution。它们共享「分配份额」的意思。

items.example: The stem appears unchanged in tribute and tributary.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干在 tribute 与 tributary 中保持不变。

items.example: Military, ordinary and tributary all use it.
The city paid tribute for decades.

items.meaning: to give a share toward a common fund
items.example: Everyone contributed a few coins.
Her contribution changed the project.
items.exampleCN: 她的贡献改变了这个项目。

items.example: Volunteers distributed the supplies.
The map shows the distribution of rainfall.
items.exampleCN: 地图显示了降雨的分布。

items.meaning: a subordinate state that pays tribute
items.example: The tributary state kept its own ruler.
items.exampleCN: 这个属国保留了自己的统治者。

items.meaning: the network of tribute relations around a powerful centre
items.meaningCN: 围绕强权中心形成的朝贡关系网络
items.example: Historians debate how far the tributary system reached.
items.exampleCN: 历史学家争论朝贡体系影响范围有多远。

latinEntries.meaning: a division of the Roman people

latinEntries.structure: tribuere, tribuo, tribui, tributus (verb, third conjugation)

definition_en: the ground over which a river flows
core_image: 河水退去后露出的那条凹槽，砾石、沙和旧水道刻出的沟
scene: 旱季水退，河中央露出一条布满砾石的凹槽，孩子们在上面捡石头。The dry riverbed was warm under their feet.
sceneCN: 这里 riverbed 指「河床」（第 1 个义项：河水流动所覆盖的河道底部）；句意为干涸的河床在他们脚下发烫。

pos.zh: 河床；河道底部（可数，复数 riverbeds）

derivatives.zh: river（复合词 riverbed 的前项，经法语上溯拉丁 ripa「岸」）→ 河；河流
riparius（拉丁「河岸的」）+ -ine（拉丁形容词后缀）→ 属于河流或河岸的：河边的
river + bank（复合，无后缀；bank 属日耳曼语）→ 河岸
river + front（复合，无后缀）→ 临河的一面：滨河地带
river + boat（复合，无后缀）→ 河上航行的船：内河船

senses.title: The ground beneath a river
senses.titleCN: 河床：河水底下的地面
senses.definition: the ground over which a river flows
senses.definitionCN: 河水在其上流过的地面
senses.example: The dry riverbed was warm under their feet.
senses.exampleCN: 干涸的河床在他们脚下发烫。
senses.why: river names the watercourse and bed names the surface it lies on, exactly as a person lies on a bed.
senses.whyCN: river 命名水道，bed 命名它所躺卧的表面，正如人躺在床之上。

senses.title: The sediment layer that forms the bed
senses.titleCN: 河床沉积层：砾石与沙构成的那一层
senses.definition: the layer of gravel, sand and silt that the river deposits as its bed
senses.definitionCN: 河流沉积而成、作为河床的砾石、沙与淤泥层
senses.example: Gravel from the riverbed is quarried for concrete.
senses.exampleCN: 河床的砾石被开采用于混凝土。
senses.why: the bed is not bare rock but the sediment the river itself deposits, so the word names both the surface and the material that makes it.
senses.whyCN: 河床并非裸露岩石，而是河流自己沉积的泥沙，因此这个词既命名表面，也命名构成它的材料。

senses.title: The exposed bed of a dry river
senses.titleCN: 干涸河床：断流后露出的河道
senses.definition: the channel bottom left exposed when a river stops flowing
senses.definitionCN: 河流断流后裸露出来的河道底部
senses.example: In August the riverbed carries no water at all.
senses.exampleCN: 到了八月，河床里一滴水也没有。
senses.why: when the water is gone the bed becomes a visible surface, and the compound then names a place you can walk on.
senses.whyCN: 水退之后，河床成为可见的表面，这个复合词于是命名一个可以行走的地方。

senses.title: The shape or profile of a channel bottom
senses.titleCN: 河床形态：河道底部的起伏与剖面
senses.definition: the form of a channel bottom, including pools, bars and riffles
senses.definitionCN: 河道底部的形态，包括深潭、边滩与浅滩
senses.example: The riverbed profile records centuries of erosion and deposition.
senses.exampleCN: 河床剖面记录了数百年的侵蚀与沉积。
senses.why: geomorphology measures the bottom as a shape, with pools and bars, so the word shifts from material to form.
senses.whyCN: 地貌学把河底当作一种形状来测量，包括深潭与边滩，于是词义从材料转到形态。

senses.title: The bed as habitat
senses.titleCN: 河床作为栖息地
senses.definition: the bottom environment considered as habitat for plants and animals
senses.definitionCN: 作为动植物栖息环境的河道底部
senses.example: Mussels burrow into the riverbed and filter the water.
senses.exampleCN: 贻贝钻进河床，过滤河水。
senses.why: ecology asks what lives on the bottom, and the same surface becomes a habitat rather than a geological feature.
senses.whyCN: 生态学追问什么生活在底部，同一表面便成为栖息地，而非地质特征。

senses.title: Bed material used in engineering
senses.titleCN: 工程用河床材料
senses.definition: the gravel, sand or stone taken from or laid on a riverbed
senses.definitionCN: 从河床取出或铺在河床上的砾石、沙或石块
senses.example: Engineers reinforced the riverbed with stone to protect the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用石块加固河床以保护桥梁。
senses.why: engineering treats the bed as a supply of material or as a surface to be strengthened, so the word names a resource and a works site.
senses.whyCN: 工程把河床当作材料来源或需要加固的表面，于是这个词命名资源与施工面。

senses.title: Long-term change of a channel bottom
senses.titleCN: 河床演变：下切、抬升与迁移
senses.definition: the slow change of a channel bottom through erosion or deposition
senses.definitionCN: 河道底部因侵蚀或沉积而缓慢发生的变化
senses.example: Damming the river caused the riverbed below it to deepen.
senses.exampleCN: 筑坝使坝下河床加深。
senses.why: when the bed is watched over decades it becomes a process: it deepens, rises and shifts as sediment moves.
senses.whyCN: 把河床放在数十年的尺度上看，它就成了一个过程：随泥沙移动而加深、抬高、迁移。

senses.title: A base on which something moves
senses.titleCN: 比喻：承载一切的基底
senses.definition: the underlying base along which something else travels or develops
senses.definitionCN: 其他事物在其上移动或发展的底层基础
senses.example: Memory is the riverbed through which every later experience flows.
senses.exampleCN: 记忆是河床，后来的每一段经历都从其中流过。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the geography: a channel lies below and gives direction to whatever flows through it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了地理关系：底部的沟槽给流经之物以方向。

intro.en: Riverbed is a transparent English compound: river came through Anglo-French from Latin ripa 'bank', and bed goes back to Old English bedd 'sleeping place'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: riverbed 是透明的英语复合词：river 经盎格鲁法语上溯拉丁 ripa「河岸」，bed 上承古英语 bedd「卧处」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bedd meant a sleeping place and was already used for the bottom of a hollow. The extension to a river bottom treats the water as something lying on a bed.
items.cn: bedd 指卧处，也已用于凹陷的底部。扩展到河底，是把水当作躺在床上的东西。

items.en: Ripa meant a bank or shore. Its adjective riparius and the Vulgar Latin derivative riparia passed through French as riviere, the source of English river.
items.cn: ripa 意为河岸或岸。其形容词 riparius 与通俗拉丁衍生词 riparia 经法语作 riviere，成为英语 river 的来源。

items.en: River and bed combine in English without change of form; the compound names the bed of a river just as seabed names the bed of the sea.
items.cn: river 与 bed 在英语中直接组合，形式不变；这个复合词命名河之床，正如 seabed 命名海之床。

items.en: The compound enters geological writing in the nineteenth century, when channel forms, bed load and river profiles became objects of measurement.
items.cn: 这个复合词在 19 世纪进入地质文献，当时河道形态、推移质与河流剖面成为测量对象。

items.en: The twentieth century adds engineering and ecological uses: bed stabilization, bed material, and the bed as habitat.
items.cn: 20 世纪增添了工程与生态用法：河床加固、河床材料，以及作为栖息地的河床。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the components are well documented, but the first written use of the compound is dated variously.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：两个构词成分均有明确记载，但复合词的最早书证年代各家著录不一。

note.en: Group one holds the parts and neighbours of a river channel; group two holds the beds of other water bodies.
note.cn: 第一组是河道的组成部分与邻近说法；第二组是其他水体的底部。

entries.definition: The land along the edge of a river; the riverbed is below the water, the bank is beside it.
entries.definitionCN: 沿河边缘的土地；河床在水下，河岸在旁边。

entries.definition: The flowing water and its channel; the bed is the ground that carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 流动的水及其水道；河床是承载它的地面。

entries.definition: The passage through which water flows, including its banks and bed; a riverbed is only the bottom.
entries.definitionCN: 水流经的整个通道，包括岸与底；riverbed 只是底部。

entries.definition: Any bottom layer or resting surface; riverbed narrows it to a watercourse.
entries.definitionCN: 任何底层或承托面；riverbed 把它收窄到水道。

entries.definition: The bottom of the sea, formed like a riverbed by sediment and currents.
entries.definitionCN: 海底，像河床一样由沉积物与水流形成。

entries.definition: The bottom of a lake, often exposed when the water level falls.
entries.definitionCN: 湖底，水位下降时常露出。

entries.definition: The bottom of a small stream, usually shallower and coarser than a riverbed.
entries.definitionCN: 小溪的底部，通常比河床更浅、颗粒更粗。

entries.definition: The flat land beside a river that floods; it lies next to the bed rather than under it.
entries.definitionCN: 河边会泛滥的平地；它在河床旁边而非下面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real neighbours, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与邻近词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: river + bed: the river lies on its bed as a person lies on a bed.
normal.cn: river + bed：河流躺在自己的床上，正如人躺在床上。

normal.en: seabed, lakebed and streambed follow the same pattern: body of water + bed.
normal.cn: seabed、lakebed、streambed 遵循同一模式：水体 + bed。

normal.en: The bed is both a surface and a material: gravel and sand are the bed itself, not just what lies on it.
normal.cn: 河床既是表面也是材料：砾石与沙本身就是河床，而不只是铺在上面的东西。

normal.en: A dry riverbed is still a riverbed; the compound names the place, not the water.
normal.cn: 干涸的河床仍然是河床；这个复合词命名地点，而非水。

normal.en: Hydrologists separate bed from bank and from floodplain, because each stores and moves water differently.
normal.cn: 水文学家把河床与河岸、河漫滩分开，因为三者蓄水与输水方式不同。

abstract.en: A riverbed is a record written in gravel: each flood leaves a line.
abstract.cn: 河床是用砾石写成的记录：每一场洪水都留下一行。

abstract.en: Memory works like a riverbed: later events cut into it and leave new deposits.
abstract.cn: 记忆像河床：后来的事件在其上切割，又留下新的沉积。

abstract.en: The bed of a dried river still shows where the water used to go.
abstract.cn: 干涸河流的河床仍显示水曾经走过的路线。

examples.en: The riverbed was exposed during the drought.
examples.cn: 干旱期间河床露了出来。

examples.en: Sediment on the riverbed shows how the current has shifted.
examples.cn: 河床上的沉积物显示水流如何改变。

examples.en: Concrete was laid to keep the riverbed from eroding.
examples.cn: 铺设混凝土以防止河床侵蚀。

dict_mnemonic.text: river（河）+ bed（床）＝河躺着的床；看到 riverbed 先想「水下的地面」，再扩展到干河床、河床材料与比喻基底。

root: 英语本族复合词，由 river（河，经古法语上溯拉丁 ripa「岸」）与 bed（床，古英语 bedd）直接组合。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of riverbed. One physical fact generates them all: water lies on ground, the ground is made of what the water carries, and anything traveling can be said to have such a bed.
sensesIntro.cn: riverbed 的八个义项。一个自然事实衍生出全部：水躺在地面上，地面由水搬运来的东西构成，而任何行进之物都可以说有这样一张床。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a channel cut into the ground, filled with moving water and loose stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：切入地面的沟槽，里面是流动的水与松散的石头。

branches.en: SURFACE AND EXPOSURE: the bottom under water, then the same bottom when the water is gone.
branches.cn: 表面与显露：先是水下的底部，再是水退后露出的同一底部。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND FORM OVER TIME: the sediment, its profile, and its slow change.
branches.cn: 材料与时间中的形态：沉积层、其剖面，以及缓慢的变化。

branches.en: LIFE ON THE BOTTOM: the bed read as habitat rather than as geology.
branches.cn: 底部生命：把河床读作栖息地，而非地质构造。

branches.en: BED AS RESOURCE: gravel and stone taken from it or laid on it.
branches.cn: 作为资源的河床：从中取出或铺上的砾石与石块。

branches.en: METAPHOR OF SUPPORT: any underlying channel that carries and directs what flows.
branches.cn: 承载隐喻：任何托住并引导流动之物的底层沟槽。

intro.en: Riverbed carries no affix at all: it is a plain compound of two free words, and its parts keep their own meanings.
intro.cn: riverbed 完全不带词缀：它由两个自由词直接复合，两部分各自保留原义。

latinIntro.en: The first half, river, goes back through French to Latin ripa 'bank', whose adjective riparius gives English riparian. The second half, bed, is Germanic and has no Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 前半 river 经法语上溯拉丁 ripa「岸」，其形容词 riparius 给出英语 riparian；后半 bed 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: a large natural stream of water
items.example: The river runs south through the plain.

items.meaning: a resting surface or bottom layer
items.example: The bed of the stream was thick with mud.
Riverine plants line the channel.
items.exampleCN: 河流植物排列在河道两侧。

items.example: Riparian rights govern use of the water.
Willows grow along the riverbank.
The riverbed was dry in late summer.

items.meaning: coarse material carried along the bed
items.meaningCN: 沿河床搬运的粗颗粒物质
items.example: Bed load moves only during high flow.
items.exampleCN: 推移质只在流量大时移动。

items.meaningCN: 松散沉积层之下的基岩
items.example: The drill reached bedrock at ten metres.
items.exampleCN: 钻头在十米处打到基岩。

latinEntries.meaning: of a bank, growing by a bank

definition_en: the land along the side of a river
core_image: 河水贴着一条长满草的斜坡流过，坡上柳树成行
scene: 春天水涨，柳树的根泡在水里，孩子们沿着草坡追着鸭子跑。Willows line the riverbank where the ducks nest.
sceneCN: 这里 riverbank 指「河岸」（第 1 个义项：紧挨河水的两侧斜坡地带）；句意为柳树排列在鸭子筑巢的河岸上。

pos.zh: 河岸；河边土地（可数，复数 riverbanks）

derivatives.zh: river（复合词 riverbank 的前项，经法语上溯拉丁 ripa「岸」）→ 河；河流
riparius（拉丁「河岸的」）+ -ine（拉丁形容词后缀）→ 属于河流或河岸的：河边的
rip-（拉丁 ripa「岸」）+ -arian（拉丁 -arius 的形容词形式）→ 属于河岸的：滨河的
river + bed（复合，无后缀）→ 河床
river + front（复合，无后缀）→ 临河的一面：滨河地带

senses.title: The land along the edge of a river
senses.titleCN: 河岸：紧挨河水的两侧地带
senses.definition: the strip of land that borders a river
senses.definitionCN: 与河流相邻的那条土地
senses.example: Willows line the riverbank where the ducks nest.
senses.exampleCN: 柳树排列在鸭子筑巢的河岸上。
senses.why: bank names a raised edge, and river supplies the water it edges; the compound is simply the edge of that water.
senses.whyCN: bank 命名隆起的边沿，river 提供它所镶边的那条水；复合词就是这条水的边沿。

senses.title: The sloping face of the bank
senses.titleCN: 河岸斜坡：从岸顶到水面的斜面
senses.definition: the slope between the top of the bank and the water
senses.definitionCN: 岸顶到水面之间的斜坡
senses.example: The riverbank collapsed after three days of rain.
senses.exampleCN: 连下三天雨之后河岸崩塌了。
senses.why: the bank is not a line but a slope, and erosion or collapse always happens on that face.
senses.whyCN: 河岸不是一条线而是一面坡，侵蚀或崩塌总是发生在坡面上。

senses.title: Land beside the river used for farming
senses.titleCN: 河边土地：沿岸的农田
senses.definition: the fields or plots that lie along a river and rely on it
senses.definitionCN: 沿河分布、依赖河流的田地
senses.example: The riverbank fields flood every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 河边的田地每年春天都被淹。
senses.why: people farm the strip because floodwater renews its soil, so the edge becomes agricultural land.
senses.whyCN: 人们耕种这条地带，因为洪水更新它的土壤，于是边缘成为农田。

senses.title: The vegetation belt of a bank
senses.titleCN: 滨河植被带：岸边的草木群落
senses.definition: the plants that grow along a river edge as a continuous strip
senses.definitionCN: 沿河岸连续生长的植物带
senses.example: The riverbank supports reeds, willows and nesting birds.
senses.exampleCN: 河岸供养着芦苇、柳树与筑巢的鸟。
senses.why: the bank is a boundary between water and land, and that boundary is where a distinct plant community grows.
senses.whyCN: 河岸是水与陆的边界，而这条边界正是独特植物群落生长之处。

senses.title: The urban riverside
senses.titleCN: 城市滨河空间：河岸上的步道与公园
senses.definition: the part of a town laid out along a river for walking and leisure
senses.definitionCN: 城镇沿河布置、供步行与休闲的地带
senses.example: A promenade runs along the riverbank in the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 老城的河岸上有一条滨河步道。
senses.why: cities turn the same strip into promenades, parks and views, so the physical edge becomes public space.
senses.whyCN: 城市把同一条地带变成步道、公园与景观，于是物理边缘成为公共空间。

senses.title: Riparian rights in law
senses.titleCN: 法律上的河岸权
senses.definition: the rights of an owner whose land borders a river, especially to use its water
senses.definitionCN: 土地与河流相邻者享有的权利，尤其用水权
senses.example: Riparian owners may not divert the river without permission.
senses.exampleCN: 河岸土地所有者未经许可不得引走河水。
senses.why: law borrows the physical edge to mark who holds rights over the water beside it.
senses.whyCN: 法律借物理上的边沿来标记谁对旁边的水享有权利。

senses.title: Bank protection works
senses.titleCN: 护岸工程：防止河岸被冲垮
senses.definition: the structures built to stop a bank from eroding
senses.definitionCN: 为防止河岸侵蚀而建的构筑物
senses.example: Stone walls protect the riverbank near the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 石墙保护桥附近的河岸。
senses.why: once the bank is property and infrastructure, the word also names the works built to keep it from washing away.
senses.whyCN: 一旦河岸成为财产与基础设施，这个词也命名防止它被冲走的工程。

senses.title: A margin or borderline
senses.titleCN: 比喻：边缘、临界地带
senses.definition: a position at the edge of something larger, neither inside nor fully outside
senses.definitionCN: 处在更大事物边缘、既不在内也不完全在外的位置
senses.example: The old factory stood on the riverbank of the new economy.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老厂站在新经济的河岸上。
senses.why: the metaphor uses the bank as the strip where two domains meet without merging.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把河岸当作两个领域相接却不相融的那条地带。

intro.en: Riverbank joins river, which came through French from Latin ripa 'bank', to bank, a word for a raised edge that English took from Old Norse. The compound is modern and transparent. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: riverbank 把 river（经法语上溯拉丁 ripa「岸」）与 bank（英语从古诺斯语借入、指隆起的边沿）并置。这个复合词是近代的，构词透明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old Norse bakki meant a ridge or the edge of a river; English bank in the river sense is generally traced to this source rather than to the financial sense.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 bakki 指土埂或河岸；英语表示河岸的 bank 一般认为来自这一支，而非金融义那一支。

items.en: Latin ripa 'bank, shore' gave riparius and Vulgar Latin riparia, which passed through Old French riviere into English river.
items.cn: 拉丁 ripa「岸」给出 riparius 与通俗拉丁 riparia，再经古法语 riviere 进入英语作 river。

items.en: River plus bank is formed inside English and needs no affix; the same pattern gives seashore and lakeshore.
items.cn: river 加 bank 在英语内部构成，无需词缀；同一模式还给出 seashore 与 lakeshore。

items.en: Nineteenth-century water law made riparian a technical term for owners of land bordering a river, and riverbank acquired legal force.
items.cn: 19 世纪水法使 riparian 成为河岸土地所有者的技术术语，riverbank 也随之带上法律含义。

items.en: Late twentieth-century ecology treats the riverbank as a buffer strip that filters runoff and supports wildlife.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期生态学把河岸视为过滤径流、供养野生动物的缓冲带。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the components are securely documented, but the compound's earliest citation is dated differently in different references.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：两个成分均有可靠记载，但复合词的最早书证各家年代不一。

note.en: Group one separates bank from the other words for edges of water; group two holds the modern terms for the riverside as a place.
note.cn: 第一组区分 bank 与表示水边的其他词；第二组是命名滨河地带的现代说法。

entries.definition: A raised edge of a river, but also the institution that holds money; context decides.
entries.definitionCN: 既可指隆起的河岸，也可指保管钱财的机构；由上下文判断。

entries.definition: The land at the edge of a sea or lake; a riverbank is specifically along a river.
entries.definitionCN: 海或湖边的陆地；riverbank 特指沿河的地带。

entries.definition: The land along a sea, considered as a region rather than a strip of bank.
entries.definitionCN: 沿海陆地，被视为一个区域而非一条岸带。

entries.definition: The sandy or pebbly slope at the edge of water; it stresses material, not ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 水边由沙或卵石构成的坡面；强调材质，而非权属。

entries.definition: The land beside any body of water, used especially of property and leisure.
entries.definitionCN: 任何水体旁的土地，尤用于房产与休闲语境。

entries.definition: The built-up strip of a town facing water, often redeveloped for housing or tourism.
entries.definitionCN: 城镇面向水体的建成地带，常被改造为住宅或旅游区。

entries.definition: The flat land beside a river that is covered in floods; it lies beyond the bank itself.
entries.definitionCN: 河边在洪水时被淹没的平地；它位于河岸之外。

entries.definition: The strip of vegetation and soil influenced by a river, treated as one functional unit.
entries.definitionCN: 受河流影响的植被与土壤带，被视为一个功能单元。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real legal terms and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词、法律术语与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: river + bank: the bank is the raised edge the river runs against.
normal.cn: river + bank：河岸就是河水流过时抵着的那道隆起边沿。

normal.en: Bank has two lives: money bank and river bank. Only the second is a riverbank.
normal.cn: bank 有两个身份：银行与河岸。只有后者构成 riverbank。

normal.en: Riparian is the formal adjective: riparian rights, riparian vegetation, riparian zone.
normal.cn: riparian 是正式形容词：河岸权、河岸植被、滨河带。

normal.en: The bank is above the water and the bed is below it; the two are never the same surface.
normal.cn: 河岸在水面之上，河床在水面之下，二者从来不是同一个表面。

normal.en: A steep riverbank collapses; a gentle one accumulates soil. The adjective predicts the process.
normal.cn: 陡岸会崩塌，缓岸会积土；形容词预示了过程。

abstract.en: Every river carries its own edge; the bank is where the water stops being water.
abstract.cn: 每条河都带着自己的边沿；河岸就是水不再只是水的地方。

abstract.en: To stand on the riverbank of a new field is to be close enough to watch and far enough to be safe.
abstract.cn: 站在新领域的河岸上，就是近到可以观察、远到仍然安全。

abstract.en: A bank erodes quietly for years and then disappears in one flood.
abstract.cn: 河岸会静静侵蚀多年，然后在一场洪水中消失。

examples.en: The riverbank was muddy after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后河岸一片泥泞。

examples.en: They planted trees along the riverbank to stop erosion.
examples.cn: 他们沿河岸种树以防侵蚀。

examples.en: A path follows the riverbank for several kilometres.
examples.cn: 一条小路沿河岸延伸数公里。

dict_mnemonic.text: river（河）+ bank（岸）＝河靠着的那道边；记住 bank 的两义（银行、河岸），再看 riparian 就明白这是法律与生态共用的「滨河带」。

root: 英语复合词，由 river（河，经古法语上溯拉丁 ripa「岸」）与 bank（岸，一般上溯古诺斯语 bakki「土埂、河岸」）组合。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of riverbank. From a physical edge, the word moves to the slope, the farmland, the vegetation strip, the urban promenade, the legal rights attached to the land, the works built to hold it, and finally any margin.
sensesIntro.cn: riverbank 的八个义项。从一个物理边沿出发，依次转到斜坡、农田、植被带、城市滨河步道、附着于土地的法律权利、护岸工程，最后是任何边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strip of grass and roots holding the land where the water pushes against it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条草与根须组成的带子，在水推挤之处稳住土地。

branches.en: THE LAND ITSELF: the bordering strip, then the fields that use it.
branches.cn: 土地本身：先是镶边的地带，再是靠它耕种的田地。

branches.en: A SLOPE THAT FAILS OR IS HELD: the bank face, then the works that keep it in place.
branches.cn: 会崩或被稳住的斜坡：先是岸面，再是使它固定的工程。

branches.en: THE LIVING STRIP: reeds, willows and nesting birds as a continuous belt.
branches.cn: 有生命的带子：芦苇、柳树与筑巢的鸟连成一条带。

branches.en: THE CITY EDGE: the bank turned into promenade, park and view.
branches.cn: 城市边缘：河岸变成步道、公园与景观。

branches.en: RIGHTS AND METAPHOR: legal claims over the edge, then any borderline position.
branches.cn: 权利与隐喻：先是针对这条边沿的法律主张，再是任何临界位置。

intro.en: Riverbank is a plain compound of two free words; it takes no prefix or suffix of its own, though both halves support large families.
intro.cn: riverbank 是两个自由词的直接复合，本身不带前缀或后缀，但两半都支撑着庞大的词族。

latinIntro.en: River descends from Latin ripa 'bank' through French; riparian is the direct Latin-derived adjective. Bank is Germanic and has no Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: river 经法语上溯拉丁 ripa「岸」；riparian 是由拉丁直接派生的形容词。bank 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。

items.example: The river bends west below the town.
items.exampleCN: 河流在城镇下方折向西。

items.meaning: a raised edge of land beside water
items.example: He sat on the bank and watched the boats.
Riparian vegetation shades the water.
A riverine forest follows the channel.
items.exampleCN: 一片滨河森林沿河道延伸。

items.example: The riverbank is steep here.

items.meaning: the built edge of a town facing a river
items.meaningCN: 城镇面向河流的建成边缘
items.example: The riverfront was redeveloped as a park.
items.exampleCN: 滨河地带被改造成公园。

items.meaning: a raised wall or mound holding back water
items.example: The embankment protects the low town.
items.exampleCN: 堤岸保护着低处的城镇。

items.meaning: the wearing away of a river bank
items.example: Bank erosion threatens the road.

definition_zh: 瀑布；跌水；瀑布般倾泻；（界面）瀑布流
definition_en: a place where a river drops over a steep edge
core_image: 河水走到岩壁尽头，整片跌下去，底部腾起白雾
scene: 山道尽头，河水从黑色岩壁上整片跌下，谷底腾起白雾。The waterfall feeds a cold pool at the foot of the cliff.
sceneCN: 这里 waterfall 指「瀑布」（第 1 个义项：河水越过陡崖整片跌落之处）；句意为这道瀑布在崖脚汇成一汪冷水潭。

pos.zh: 瀑布；跌水；瀑布状倾泻（可数，复数 waterfalls）
瀑布式的（多用于复合术语，如瀑布模型）

derivatives.zh: waterfall + model（复合术语，无后缀）→ 像瀑布一样逐级下落的开发流程：瀑布模型
waterfall + chart（复合术语，无后缀）→ 逐项增减如跌水的图表：瀑布图
waterfall + layout（复合术语，无后缀）→ 页面元素像水帘层层排布的布局：瀑布流布局

senses.title: A natural fall of a river
senses.titleCN: 天然瀑布：河水整片跌落
senses.definition: a place where a river drops steeply over a rock edge
senses.definitionCN: 河流越过岩石陡坎整片跌落的地点
senses.example: The waterfall feeds a cold pool at the foot of the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 这道瀑布在崖脚汇成一汪冷水潭。
senses.why: water and fall are simply placed side by side: the word names water in the act of falling.
senses.whyCN: water 与 fall 直接并置：这个词命名「正在落下的水」。

senses.title: An artificial drop in a channel
senses.titleCN: 人工跌水：水利工程中的落差
senses.definition: a built step in a canal or channel where water drops to a lower level
senses.definitionCN: 渠道中人工建造、使水降到低处的落差
senses.example: A waterfall in the canal breaks the speed of the flow.
senses.exampleCN: 渠中的一处跌水减缓了流速。
senses.why: a canal repeats the natural drop in concrete, and the same word covers the built step because the shape is identical.
senses.whyCN: 运河用混凝土重复自然的落差，同样的词覆盖人工跌水，因为形状一致。

senses.title: The falling sheet of water
senses.titleCN: 瀑布水帘：跌落的那片水
senses.definition: the body of water itself as it falls, rather than the place
senses.definitionCN: 跌落中的水体本身，而非地点
senses.example: Mist rose where the waterfall struck the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 瀑布击打岩石处腾起水雾。
senses.why: the place and the water in it are separable in thought, so the word can name the falling sheet itself.
senses.whyCN: 地点与其中的水在思维上可以分开，因此这个词能命名跌落的水帘本身。

senses.title: A waterfall as scenery
senses.titleCN: 瀑布景观：作为观赏对象
senses.definition: a waterfall viewed as a landscape feature or visitor attraction
senses.definitionCN: 被当作景观或游览对象的瀑布
senses.example: The waterfall draws thousands of visitors each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这道瀑布每年夏天吸引数千游客。
senses.why: tourism turns the fall into an object to be visited, and the word then names the attraction rather than the drop.
senses.whyCN: 旅游把瀑布变成被参观的对象，于是这个词命名景点而非落差。

senses.title: A series of falls
senses.titleCN: 多级瀑布：一级级跌落的瀑布群
senses.definition: a succession of drops along one river, treated as a single feature
senses.definitionCN: 同一条河上连续的多级跌落，被视为一个景观
senses.example: A series of waterfalls steps down the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 一串瀑布沿山谷逐级而下。
senses.why: a staircase of drops is still one feature, so the singular word extends to a whole series.
senses.whyCN: 一串阶梯式落差仍是一个景观，因此单数词扩展到整组瀑布。

senses.title: Retreat of a waterfall by erosion
senses.titleCN: 瀑布后退：陡坎被侵蚀向上游移动
senses.definition: the upstream movement of a fall as the rock lip is eroded
senses.definitionCN: 岩石坎唇被侵蚀，使瀑布位置向上游移动
senses.example: The waterfall retreats upstream as the lip wears back.
senses.exampleCN: 坎唇被磨退，瀑布便向上游后退。
senses.why: the fall is not fixed: its lip erodes and the whole feature migrates upstream, which geology records as retreat.
senses.whyCN: 瀑布并不固定：坎唇被侵蚀，整个景观向上游迁移，地质学称之为后退。

senses.title: Anything falling in sheets
senses.titleCN: 比喻：瀑布般倾泻的事物
senses.definition: a large amount of something that seems to fall continuously
senses.definitionCN: 大量事物像水一样连续倾泻
senses.example: A waterfall of light poured through the high window.
senses.exampleCN: 一片光像瀑布一样从高窗倾泻进来。
senses.why: anything that falls in a continuous sheet shares the shape of the water, so the word becomes a metaphor for abundance.
senses.whyCN: 任何连续成片落下之物都共享水的形状，于是这个词成为「丰沛倾泻」的比喻。

senses.title: Waterfall layout or chart
senses.titleCN: 专名：瀑布流布局与瀑布图
senses.definition: a layout in which columns of uneven height flow downward, or a chart of successive gains and losses
senses.definitionCN: 高度不齐的栏目向下流动的排版，或逐项显示增减的图表
senses.example: The gallery uses a waterfall layout on small screens.
senses.exampleCN: 这个画廊在小屏幕上采用瀑布流布局。
senses.why: both computing uses keep the image of separate streams falling into place one after another.
senses.whyCN: 两种计算用法都保留了「一股股水流依次落下归位」的意象。

intro.en: Waterfall is a native English compound of water and fall. Water goes back to Old English wæter, and fall to Old English feallan 'to fall'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: waterfall 是英语本族复合词，由 water 与 fall 构成。water 上承古英语 wæter，fall 上承古英语 feallan「落下」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wæter is the Germanic word for water, with German Wasser and Dutch water as close relatives.
items.cn: wæter 是日耳曼语的水词，德语 Wasser 与荷兰语 water 是近亲。

items.en: Feallan meant to fall or drop; the noun fall was formed from the same verb and covers both a season and an act of falling.
items.cn: feallan 意为落下、跌落；名词 fall 由同一动词构成，兼指季节与下落动作。

items.en: Water plus fall is recorded in the modern sense from the sixteenth century, when travellers described steep drops in mountain rivers.
items.cn: water 加 fall 的现代义在 16 世纪有记录，当时游记描述山间河流的陡落。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geologists explain waterfall retreat, caprock and plunge pools, fixing the technical vocabulary.
items.cn: 19 世纪地质学家解释瀑布后退、盖岩与跌水潭，固定了技术词汇。

items.en: The twentieth century adds the waterfall model in software engineering and the waterfall chart in finance; web design adds the waterfall layout.
items.cn: 20 世纪软件工程增添了 waterfall model，金融增添了 waterfall chart；网页设计又增添了 waterfall layout。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the two parts are securely documented, but the compound's earliest citation varies between references.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：两个成分均有可靠记载，但复合词的最早书证各家著录不同。

note.en: Group one holds other water compounds that are easy to swap; group two holds the words for different kinds of falling water.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混淆的其他 water 复合词；第二组是各种跌落水体的说法。

entries.definition: Birds that live on or near water; the second element is fowl, not fall.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在水上或水边的鸟；第二成分是 fowl，不是 fall。

entries.definition: The ridge between drainage basins, or the basin itself; nothing falls in it.
entries.definitionCN: 流域之间的分水岭，或指流域本身；其中并没有水落下。

entries.definition: A river or canal used for travel or transport; it names a path, not a drop.
entries.definitionCN: 用于航行或运输的河或运河；它命名路径，而非落差。

entries.definition: A wheel turned by flowing water; the second element is wheel.
entries.definitionCN: 由流水推动的轮子；第二成分是 wheel。

entries.definition: A small waterfall, or a series of them, often in a garden or a mountain stream.
entries.definitionCN: 小瀑布或一串小瀑布，常见于园林或山溪。

entries.definition: A very large or powerful waterfall; the word is also used for an eye condition.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大或有力的瀑布；该词也指一种眼病。

entries.definition: A stretch of fast, turbulent water over rocks, without a sheer fall.
entries.definitionCN: 水流湍急、越过岩石的一段河面，但没有陡直落差。

entries.definition: A waterfall or series of waterfalls, often in proper names such as Niagara Falls.
entries.definitionCN: 瀑布或瀑布群，常用于专名，如尼亚加拉瀑布。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: water + fall: the word is a picture of water falling.
normal.cn: water + fall：这个词就是「水在落」的一幅画。

normal.en: Waterfall, watershed and waterway all begin with water but end in different directions: falling, dividing, travelling.
normal.cn: waterfall、watershed、waterway 都以 water 开头，却分别落在落、分、行三个方向。

normal.en: A waterfall retreats upstream; the lip wears back and the fall moves with it.
normal.cn: 瀑布向上游后退：坎唇磨退，瀑布便跟着移动。

normal.en: The plunge pool at the foot is the basin the falling water digs.
normal.cn: 崖脚的跌水潭就是落水自己挖出的盆。

normal.en: Waterfall model, chart and layout are all visual descents, one after another.
normal.cn: 瀑布模型、瀑布图与瀑布流布局都是「一级接一级落下」的视觉比喻。

abstract.en: A waterfall is a river deciding, at one edge, to become air for a moment.
abstract.cn: 瀑布是一条河在某个边沿决定暂时变成空气。

abstract.en: Good news can arrive as a waterfall, all at once, after a long dry season.
abstract.cn: 好消息可以像瀑布一样，在漫长的旱季之后一次倾泻而下。

abstract.en: A waterfall keeps moving upstream while seeming to stand still, like a habit wearing away at its own source.
abstract.cn: 瀑布看似不动，却一直向上游移动，像一种习惯在磨蚀自己的源头。

examples.en: The waterfall drops thirty metres into the gorge.
examples.cn: 瀑布落差三十米，落入峡谷。

examples.en: Mist from the waterfall soaked their clothes.
examples.cn: 瀑布的水雾打湿了他们的衣服。

examples.en: Engineers built a waterfall to lower the canal by two metres.
examples.cn: 工程师建了一处跌水，使运河水位下降两米。

dict_mnemonic.text: water（水）+ fall（落）＝正在落下的水；天然瀑布、人工跌水、光帘比喻、瀑布流布局，都是「整片往下落」。

root: 英语本族复合词，由 water（水，古英语 wæter）与 fall（落下，古英语 feallan）直接组合。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of waterfall. The physical fall generates the rest: an artificial drop repeats it, the falling sheet is its body, scenery is how it is seen, retreat is how it ages, and the computing terms borrow its shape.
sensesIntro.cn: waterfall 的八个义项。自然瀑布衍生其余各义：人工跌水重复它，水帘是它的身体，景观是观看方式，后退是它变老的方式，而计算术语借用了它的形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river reaches a hard edge and pours over it into mist.
core.cn: 核心意象：河流走到坚硬的边沿，整片倾泻下去，落入水雾。

branches.en: NATURAL FALLS: one drop, then a whole staircase of drops.
branches.cn: 自然瀑布：先是一处落差，再是一整段阶梯式瀑布群。

branches.en: BUILT AND AGING DROPS: an artificial step, then the natural retreat of the lip.
branches.cn: 人造与老去的落差：先是人工跌水，再是坎唇自然后退。

branches.en: THE FALLING BODY: the water itself, seen as a sheet rather than a place.
branches.cn: 跌落的水体：把水本身看作水帘，而非地点。

branches.en: THE VIEW: the fall turned into scenery and a destination.
branches.cn: 景观：瀑布被转化为风景与目的地。

branches.en: BORROWED SHAPES: light pouring like water, and interface or chart streams falling into place.
branches.cn: 借用的形状：光像水一样倾泻，界面或图表的股流依次落下归位。

intro.en: Waterfall takes no affix: it is water plus fall, and the meaning is exactly the sum of the parts.
intro.cn: waterfall 不带词缀：它是 water 加 fall，意义正是两部分之和。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic and have no Latin cognates. Latin named a waterfall cataracta, borrowed from Greek kataraktes, and English later borrowed cataract; it is a different word, not a relative of waterfall.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。拉丁语称瀑布为 cataracta，借自希腊语 kataraktes，英语后来借入 cataract；那是另一个词，与 waterfall 没有同源关系。

items.example: Water rushed over the lip.
The fall is twenty metres high.
The waterfall is frozen in winter.

items.meaning: a software process with fixed sequential stages
items.meaningCN: 阶段固定、依次推进的软件开发流程
items.example: The team abandoned the waterfall model for shorter cycles.
items.exampleCN: 团队放弃了瀑布模型，改用更短的周期。

items.meaning: a chart showing successive increases and decreases
items.example: The waterfall chart explains the profit gap.
items.exampleCN: 瀑布图解释了利润缺口。

items.meaning: a grid whose columns flow downward at uneven heights
items.meaningCN: 各列高度不齐、向下排列的网格
items.example: The site uses a waterfall layout for photos.
items.exampleCN: 该网站用瀑布流布局展示照片。

items.meaning: the deep basin dug by falling water
items.example: Salmon rest in the plunge pool below.
items.exampleCN: 鲑鱼在下方跌水潭里歇息。

items.meaning: the hard layer that holds up a fall's lip
items.meaningCN: 托住瀑布坎唇的硬岩层
items.example: Caprock slows the retreat of the waterfall.

definition_en: a large mass of ice that forms on land and moves slowly under its own weight
core_image: 一条巨大的冰舌从山谷深处推出来，底部磨着岩石，末端滴着融水
scene: 山谷深处，一条灰白色的冰舌缓慢推出来，末端不断滴下融水。The glacier has ground the valley walls smooth.
sceneCN: 这里 glacier 指「冰川」（第 1 个义项：在陆地上形成并靠自身重量缓慢流动的巨大冰体）；句意为这条冰川把谷壁磨得光滑。

pos.zh: 冰川；冰河（可数，复数 glaciers）

derivatives.zh: glaci-（拉丁 glacies「冰」）+ -al（拉丁 -alis，表「与……有关的」）→ 冰川的；引申为极冷的
glaci-（拉丁 glacies「冰」）+ -ation（拉丁 -atio，表过程）→ 冰覆盖与流动的过程：冰川作用、冰期
glaci-（拉丁 glacies「冰」）+ -ate（拉丁 -atus，动词后缀）→ 使受冰川作用；使冻结
glacio-（冰）+ -logy（希腊 -logia，表学科）→ 研究冰与冰川的学科：冰川学
glaciology + -ist（希腊 -istēs 经拉丁 -ista，表人）→ 从事冰川研究的人

senses.title: A valley glacier
senses.titleCN: 山谷冰川：沿山谷下行的冰体
senses.definition: a mass of ice confined to a valley and flowing down it
senses.definitionCN: 被限制在山谷中并向下流动的冰体
senses.example: The glacier has ground the valley walls smooth.
senses.exampleCN: 这条冰川把谷壁磨得光滑。
senses.why: glacier names a body of ice that behaves like a very slow river: it is confined by its valley and flows in one direction.
senses.whyCN: glacier 命名一种行为像极慢河流的冰体：它被山谷约束，只朝一个方向流动。

senses.title: A continental glacier
senses.titleCN: 大陆冰川：覆盖大片陆地的冰体
senses.definition: an ice mass that spreads outward over a continent rather than down a valley
senses.definitionCN: 在陆地上向外摊开、而非沿谷下行的巨大冰体
senses.example: A continental glacier once covered the northern plains.
senses.exampleCN: 一块大陆冰川曾经覆盖北方平原。
senses.why: the same noun covers both sizes, because valley ice and continental ice share the defining behaviour of spreading under their own weight.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词覆盖两种尺度，因为谷冰川与大陆冰川共享「靠自身重量向外摊开」这一界定行为。

senses.title: The ice mass itself
senses.titleCN: 冰川体量：作为一大块冰
senses.definition: the body of ice considered as a volume, with depth and mass
senses.definitionCN: 把冰体视为有厚度与质量的体积
senses.example: The glacier is hundreds of metres thick at its centre.
senses.exampleCN: 这条冰川中心处厚达数百米。
senses.why: once the mass is measured, the word names a volume with depth, not only a moving stream.
senses.whyCN: 一旦对冰体进行测量，这个词就命名一个有厚度的体积，而不只是流动的冰河。

senses.title: The slow flow of ice
senses.titleCN: 冰川流动：冰的缓慢运动
senses.definition: the slow downhill movement of ice by internal deformation and sliding
senses.definitionCN: 冰因内部变形与底部滑动而缓慢下移
senses.example: The glacier moves about a metre a day in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天这条冰川每天大约移动一米。
senses.why: the defining behaviour is motion; without flow the same ice would be a snowfield, so the flow sense is central.
senses.whyCN: 界定性行为是运动；若不流动，同样的冰只是雪原，因此「流动」这一义是核心。

senses.title: The tongue or terminus
senses.titleCN: 冰舌与冰川末端
senses.definition: the lower end of a glacier, where it reaches a valley floor or a lake
senses.definitionCN: 冰川的下端，抵达谷底或湖泊之处
senses.example: The glacier tongue ends in a milky lake.
senses.exampleCN: 冰舌终止在一个乳白色的湖里。
senses.why: the terminus is where the glacier becomes visible as an edge, so the word names that projecting end.
senses.whyCN: 末端是冰川作为边缘显现之处，因此这个词命名伸出的那一端。

senses.title: An ancient glacier
senses.titleCN: 古冰川：更新世留下的冰体与遗迹
senses.definition: a glacier of an earlier geological period, known from its deposits and landforms
senses.definitionCN: 更早地质时期的冰川，由其沉积与地貌得知
senses.example: Pleistocene glaciers carved the deep fjords.
senses.exampleCN: 更新世的冰川刻出了深峡湾。
senses.why: geology reads present landforms as the work of past ice, so the word extends backward in time.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把现存地貌读作过去冰体的作品，于是这个词向时间深处延伸。

senses.title: Glacier meltwater as a resource
senses.titleCN: 冰川融水：作为水源的冰
senses.definition: the water released by a glacier, treated as a seasonal or long-term supply
senses.definitionCN: 冰川释放的水，被视为季节性或长期水源
senses.example: Farmers below depend on glacier melt in the dry months.
senses.exampleCN: 下游农民在旱月依赖冰川融水。
senses.why: meltwater is the glacier entering the water cycle, so the same noun names a water supply.
senses.whyCN: 融水是冰川进入水循环的方式，因此同一名词也命名一种水源。

senses.title: A slow unstoppable mass
senses.titleCN: 比喻：缓慢而不可阻挡的巨大力量
senses.definition: anything enormous that advances very slowly and cannot be reversed easily
senses.definitionCN: 任何巨大、推进极慢且难以逆转的事物
senses.example: A glacier of paperwork moved through the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 一大堆文书像冰川一样在部里缓慢移动。
senses.why: the metaphor borrows two features at once: immense mass and almost invisible speed.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻同时借用了两个特征：巨大的体量与几乎看不见的速度。

intro.en: Glacier came into English from French glacier, from a Savoy dialect form of Latin glacies 'ice'. The Latin noun is the base of glacial and glaciation as well. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: glacier 经法语 glacier 进入英语，出自拉丁 glacies「冰」的萨瓦方言形式。这个拉丁名词也是 glacial 与 glaciation 的词基。年代均为约数。

items.en: Glacies meant ice, and was used of ice on water and of hard frost. Its deeper origin is often reconstructed as a root meaning cold, but the reconstruction is not universally accepted.
items.cn: glacies 意为冰，用于水面结冰与严霜。其更深来源常被重构为表示「寒冷」的词根，但这一重构未被普遍接受。

items.en: In the western Alps, speakers used a descendant of glacies for the ice rivers of the mountains; French glacier and Italian ghiacciaio both continue this local use.
items.cn: 在西阿尔卑斯山区，人们用 glacies 的后代指山中的冰河；法语 glacier 与意大利语 ghiacciaio 都延续这一地方用法。

items.en: English adopted glacier in the eighteenth century, when Alpine travel and natural history became fashionable; earlier writers used the French spelling.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪吸收 glacier，当时阿尔卑斯旅行与博物学成为风尚；更早的作者仍用法语拼写。

items.en: In the nineteenth century Agassiz and others argued that glaciers had once covered much of Europe, and glacier became a key term of geology.
items.cn: 19 世纪阿加西等人主张冰川曾经覆盖欧洲大部，glacier 成为地质学的关键术语。

items.en: In the twentieth and twenty-first centuries glacier retreat becomes a measurable indicator of warming, and glacier mass balance a standard quantity.
items.cn: 在 20 与 21 世纪，冰川退缩成为可测量的变暖指标，冰川质量平衡成为标准量。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin root of glacies is reconstructed rather than attested, and the first English date varies by a few decades between references.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：glacies 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构而非实证，英语首见年代各家著录相差数十年。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound like glacier but are not ice; group two holds the other terms for bodies of ice.
note.cn: 第一组是形音近似却与冰无关的词；第二组是其他冰体的术语。

entries.definition: A person who fits glass into windows; the ending is -ier, not -ier of glacier, and the root is glass.
entries.definitionCN: 安装窗玻璃的工人；词尾与 glacier 相似，但词根是 glass。

entries.definition: A French borrowing meaning iced or candied, used of fruit and leather; it is not a glacier.
entries.definitionCN: 借自法语，意为加冰的或糖渍的，用于水果与皮革；与冰川无关。

entries.definition: A gentle slope in fortification or geology; it looks like glacier but has a different ending.
entries.definitionCN: 防御工事或地质学中的缓坡；形似 glacier，词尾不同。

entries.definition: A grey-green or bluish-green surface, as on some leaves; it only sounds similar.
entries.definitionCN: 灰绿或蓝绿色表面，如某些叶片；只是读音相近。

entries.definition: A mass of ice covering a whole region and spreading outward; larger than a valley glacier.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖整个区域并向外摊开的冰体；比山谷冰川更大。

entries.definition: A dome of ice over a summit or polar area, smaller than an ice sheet.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖山顶或极地区域的穹状冰体，小于冰盖。

entries.definition: A rapidly moving corridor within an ice sheet, behaving like a river of ice.
entries.definitionCN: 冰盖内部快速流动的走廊，行为像一条冰河。

entries.definition: A floating chunk of ice that has broken off a glacier or ice shelf.
entries.definitionCN: 从冰川或冰架断裂、漂浮的冰块。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real roots, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根、同族词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: glacier and glacial share the Latin base glacies 'ice'; the noun ends in -ier, the adjective in -al.
normal.cn: glacier 与 glacial 共享拉丁词基 glacies「冰」；名词以 -ier 结尾，形容词以 -al 结尾。

normal.en: A glacier is a river of ice: confined, flowing, and ending in a tongue.
normal.cn: 冰川是一条冰之河：被约束、会流动、以冰舌收尾。

normal.en: Glacier retreat means the terminus moves uphill, not that the ice flows backwards.
normal.cn: 冰川退缩指末端向高处移动，而不是冰倒着流。

normal.en: Iceberg is the piece that breaks off; glacier is the mass it broke from.
normal.cn: iceberg 是断下来的那块，glacier 是它断自的那一整块。

normal.en: Glaciology, glaciologist and glaciation all keep the same glaci- stem.
normal.cn: glaciology、glaciologist、glaciation 都保留同一个 glaci- 词干。

abstract.en: A glacier is water that decided to move so slowly that stone had time to change.
abstract.cn: 冰川是水决定慢到让石头有时间改变。

abstract.en: Institutions can be glaciers: enormous, slow, and able to carve valleys before anyone notices.
abstract.cn: 机构也可能是冰川：庞大、缓慢，能在无人注意时刻出山谷。

abstract.en: A glacier is a library of old air, written in layers of snow.
abstract.cn: 冰川是一座旧空气的图书馆，以雪层写就。

examples.en: The glacier has retreated two kilometres in fifty years.
examples.cn: 这条冰川在五十年里退缩了两公里。

examples.en: Meltwater from the glacier feeds the valley's rivers.
examples.cn: 冰川融水供养着山谷里的河流。

examples.en: Debris carried by the glacier forms a long moraine.
examples.cn: 冰川搬运的岩屑形成一道长长的冰碛。

dict_mnemonic.text: glacier 来自拉丁 glacies（冰）：一条会流动的冰河；glacial 是它的形容词，glaciation 是它做过的事，glaciology 是研究它。

root: 经法语 glacier 上溯拉丁 glacies「冰」；同族词包括 glacial、glaciation、glaciology。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of glacier. The physical mass yields the rest: its size, its movement, its end, its ancient forms, its water, and finally its use as an image of slow power.
sensesIntro.cn: glacier 的八个义项。物理冰体衍生其余各义：体量、运动、末端、古代形态、融水，最后是「缓慢巨力」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white river of ice pushing down a valley, grinding the walls as it goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条白色的冰之河沿谷下行，边走边磨蚀谷壁。

branches.en: TWO SCALES: ice confined to a valley, then ice spreading over a continent.
branches.cn: 两种尺度：先是困在谷中的冰，再是铺满大陆的冰。

branches.en: MASS AND MOTION: a thick body, then the slow flow that makes it a glacier rather than a snowfield.
branches.cn: 体量与运动：先是有厚度的冰体，再是使它成为冰川而非雪原的缓慢流动。

branches.en: THE END: the tongue, where ice meets water and turns into melt.
branches.cn: 末端：冰舌处冰与水相接并化为融水。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: the same mass read in the landforms it left behind.
branches.cn: 深时：从留下的地貌读出同一冰体。

branches.en: RESOURCE AND IMAGE: meltwater as supply, then any slow unstoppable mass.
branches.cn: 资源与意象：先是作为水源的融水，再是任何缓慢而不可阻挡的巨物。

intro.en: Glacier is a borrowing, not an English derivation: it keeps the French noun ending, while its Latin base glacies supplies the adjective and the scientific family.
intro.cn: glacier 是借词而非英语派生词：它保留法语名词词尾，其拉丁词基 glacies 则供应形容词与科学词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin glacies yields glacier, glacial, glaciate, glaciation, glaciology and glaciologist. The family is one of the most regular in earth science.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 glacies 衍生 glacier、glacial、glaciate、glaciation、glaciology、glaciologist。这个词族在地球科学中最为规整。

items.example: Glacies covers the lake in winter.
The glacialis wind came off the peaks.
items.exampleCN: 冰冷的寒风从山峰吹来。

items.example: The glacier fills the upper valley.
Glacial ice is blue under compression.
items.exampleCN: 受挤压的冰川冰呈蓝色。

items.example: The plateau was glaciated twice.
items.exampleCN: 这片高原两次受到冰川作用。

items.meaning: the process or period of glacial cover
items.example: Glaciation reshaped the whole basin.
items.exampleCN: 冰川作用重塑了整个盆地。

items.example: Glaciology combines physics and geology.
items.exampleCN: 冰川学结合物理学与地质学。

items.example: A glaciologist measured the ice depth.
items.exampleCN: 一位冰川学家测量了冰的厚度。

items.meaning: the lower projecting end of a glacier
items.example: The glacier tongue reaches the lake.

definition_zh: 冰川的；冰期的；极冷的；冷淡的；极缓慢的；冰状的
definition_en: relating to glaciers or ice, and hence extremely cold, unfriendly or slow
core_image: 一整片蓝白色的冰压在石头上，冰面冷得连空气都像静止
scene: 高原的夏天，湖面仍浮着碎冰，风吹过来像从冰库里放出来的。The wind off the glacial lake cut through their coats.
sceneCN: 这里 glacial 指「冰川的、来自冰川的」（第 1 个义项：与冰川或冰体有关的）；句意为冰川湖吹来的风穿透了他们的外套。

pos.zh: 冰川的；冰期的；极冷的；冷淡的；极缓慢的；（化学）冰状的

derivatives.zh: glaci-（拉丁 glacies「冰」）+ -er（法语 -ier，源自拉丁 -arium，表事物）→ 会流动的冰体：冰川
glaci-（拉丁 glacies「冰」）+ -ation（拉丁 -atio，表过程）→ 冰覆盖与流动的过程：冰川作用、冰期
glaci-（拉丁 glacies「冰」）+ -ate（拉丁 -atus，动词后缀）→ 使受冰川作用；使冻结
glacial + -ly（古英语 -lice，副词后缀）→ 以冰川的方式；引申为冷淡地、极慢地
glacio-（冰）+ -logy（希腊 -logia，表学科）→ 研究冰与冰川的学科：冰川学

senses.title: Of glaciers or ice
senses.titleCN: 冰川的：与冰川或冰体有关的
senses.definition: relating to a glacier or to ice formed by glacial action
senses.definitionCN: 与冰川或由冰川作用形成的冰有关的
senses.example: The wind off the glacial lake cut through their coats.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川湖吹来的风穿透了他们的外套。
senses.why: glacial is the adjective of glacies 'ice', so its first duty is simply to mark anything made of or fed by ice.
senses.whyCN: glacial 是 glacies「冰」的形容词，首要职责就是标记任何由冰构成或由冰供养的事物。

senses.title: Of an ice age
senses.titleCN: 冰期的：属于冰川时期的
senses.definition: belonging to a period when ice sheets covered large areas
senses.definitionCN: 属于冰盖覆盖大片陆地的时期
senses.example: Glacial periods alternate with warmer intervals.
senses.exampleCN: 冰期与较暖的间冰期交替出现。
senses.why: geology turns the adjective into a label for a whole stretch of time, because ice cover is its defining feature.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把这个形容词变成一整段时间的标签，因为冰盖正是那段时间的界定特征。

senses.title: Extremely cold
senses.titleCN: 极冷的：温度像冰一样
senses.definition: so cold that it feels like ice
senses.definitionCN: 冷得如同冰一样
senses.example: A glacial wind swept the empty square.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵冰冷的风扫过空荡的广场。
senses.why: the physical cold of ice is transferred directly to air and water, with no metaphor beyond the temperature itself.
senses.whyCN: 冰的物理寒冷被直接移到空气与水上，除了温度本身并无额外比喻。

senses.title: Cold in manner
senses.titleCN: 冷淡的：态度像冰一样
senses.definition: unfriendly and emotionally distant in manner
senses.definitionCN: 态度不友好、情感疏远的
senses.example: She gave him a glacial stare and walked on.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷冷地看了他一眼，继续走开。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the temperature and moves it from air to feeling: a frozen manner chills the room.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了温度，只把它从空气移到情感：冰冷的态度让整个房间降温。

senses.title: Extremely slow
senses.titleCN: 极缓慢的：速度像冰川
senses.definition: proceeding at a pace as slow as a glacier
senses.definitionCN: 以像冰川一样缓慢的速度推进
senses.example: Progress on the reform was glacial.
senses.exampleCN: 改革进展极其缓慢。
senses.why: glaciers move metres a year, so glacial becomes a standard measure of almost invisible speed.
senses.whyCN: 冰川一年只移动几米，因此 glacial 成为「几乎看不见的速度」的标准说法。

senses.title: Produced by glacial action
senses.titleCN: 冰川造成的：冰川沉积与地貌
senses.definition: formed or deposited by the action of a glacier
senses.definitionCN: 由冰川作用形成或沉积的
senses.example: Glacial deposits cover the plain north of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川沉积覆盖着河以北的平原。
senses.why: in geology the adjective marks origin, not temperature: the material is glacial because a glacier put it there.
senses.whyCN: 在地质学中，这个形容词标记来源而非温度：材料之所以是 glacial，因为冰川把它放在那里。

senses.title: Ice-like in chemistry
senses.titleCN: 化学义：冰状的、无水的
senses.definition: of an acid so concentrated that it resembles ice
senses.definitionCN: 指浓到近乎冰状的酸
senses.example: Glacial acetic acid is almost pure acetic acid.
senses.exampleCN: 冰醋酸几乎是纯乙酸。
senses.why: the old chemical usage kept the literal image: the liquid is pure enough to freeze at room temperature and look like ice.
senses.whyCN: 古老的化学用法保留了字面意象：液体纯到能在室温凝固、看起来像冰。

senses.title: Carved by ice
senses.titleCN: 冰川刻蚀的：U 形谷与冰蚀地貌
senses.definition: shaped by the erosive passage of ice, as a valley or a rock surface
senses.definitionCN: 被冰的侵蚀通过所塑造，如谷地或岩面
senses.example: A glacial valley has steep sides and a broad floor.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川谷两侧陡峭、谷底宽阔。
senses.why: the valley shape is evidence of ice, so the adjective marks origin in the landform itself.
senses.whyCN: 山谷的形状就是冰的证据，因此这个形容词在景观本身中标记来源。

intro.en: Glacial comes from Latin glacialis 'icy', from glacies 'ice'. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century; the geological senses developed in the nineteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: glacial 来自拉丁 glacialis「冰的」，出 glacies「冰」。英语于 16 世纪借入；地质学各义在 19 世纪发展出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Glacies meant ice, whether on water or on a mountain. Its deeper root is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: glacies 意为冰，无论水面之冰还是山中之冰。其更深词根属重构而非实证。

items.en: Glacialis 'icy, frozen' was formed with the adjective suffix -alis; Latin could apply it to water, wind, metal and human temperament.
items.cn: glacialis「冰的、冻结的」由形容词后缀 -alis 构成；拉丁语可用它形容水、风、金属与人的性情。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English uses glacial for icy cold; the spelling and meaning come through French and directly from Latin.
items.cn: 16 世纪英语用 glacial 表示「冰冷的」；拼写与词义经法语或直接取自拉丁语。

items.en: When glacial theory was accepted in the nineteenth century, glacial acquired its technical senses of ice ages, deposits and erosion.
items.cn: 19 世纪冰川学说被接受后，glacial 获得冰期、沉积与侵蚀等技术义。

items.en: Twentieth-century English extends glacial to manner (a glacial stare) and to speed (glacial progress), both keeping the core image of ice.
items.cn: 20 世纪英语把 glacial 扩展到态度（冷淡的一瞥）与速度（极慢的进展），两者都保留冰的核心意象。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of glacies remains a reconstruction, and the first date of each transferred sense is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：glacies 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构，各引申义的首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close but are not built on ice; group two holds the cold adjectives with which glacial is often confused.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近却不以冰为词根的词；第二组是常与 glacial 混淆的寒冷形容词。

entries.definition: A worker who fits glass; its root is glass, so it has nothing to do with glaciers.
entries.definitionCN: 安装玻璃的工人；词根是 glass，与冰川无关。

entries.definition: A French word for iced or sugared fruit; the final accent and vowel separate it from glacial.
entries.definitionCN: 法语词，指糖渍或加冰的水果；重音与元音都与 glacial 不同。

entries.definition: A gentle artificial or natural slope; spelled almost like glacial but pronounced with a final s.
entries.definitionCN: 平缓的人工或天然斜坡；拼写近似 glacial，但末尾读作 s。

entries.definition: A grey-green bloom on leaves or fruit; only the opening sounds resemble glacial.
entries.definitionCN: 叶片或果实表面的灰绿色粉层；只有开头音近似 glacial。

entries.definition: Of the region around the North Pole; it names a place, while glacial names ice or coldness.
entries.definitionCN: 指北极附近地区；它命名地点，而 glacial 命名冰或寒冷。

entries.definition: Extremely cold, and in common use also meaning sexually uninterested.
entries.definitionCN: 极冷的，日常也指对性事毫无兴趣。

entries.definition: Covered with ice or as cold as ice; it is the everyday word that glacial formalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 覆冰的或冷如冰的；它是 glacial 所正式化的日常词。

entries.definition: Covered with frost, or unfriendly in manner; it concerns a thin surface, not a glacier.
entries.definitionCN: 覆霜的，或态度冷淡的；它涉及薄薄一层表面，而非冰川。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、同族词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: glacial = glaci- (ice) + -al (relating to): the adjective of ice in all its forms.
normal.cn: glacial = glaci-（冰）+ -al（与……有关）：冰在各种形态下的形容词。

normal.en: The same adjective covers cold air, a cold stare and a cold pace; the temperature image does all three jobs.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词覆盖冷空气、冷淡目光与缓慢速度；温度意象同时完成三件事。

normal.en: Glacial period and glacial lake are technical; glacial pace and glacial stare are metaphors.
normal.cn: glacial period 与 glacial lake 是专业说法；glacial pace 与 glacial stare 是比喻。

normal.en: Glacial acetic acid is named for its ice-like appearance, not for a glacier.
normal.cn: 冰醋酸的名称来自它像冰的外观，而非冰川。

normal.en: Glacier is the noun, glacial is the adjective, glaciation is the event: one stem, three jobs.
normal.cn: glacier 是名词，glacial 是形容词，glaciation 是事件：一个词干，三种职能。

abstract.en: A glacial silence is a silence with a temperature.
abstract.cn: 冰川般的沉默是有温度的沉默。

abstract.en: Bureaucracies can move at a glacial pace and still reshape a country over a century.
abstract.cn: 官僚机构能以冰川般的速度前进，却仍在一个世纪里重塑一个国家。

abstract.en: The glacial past is still in the soil, in the shape of every valley.
abstract.cn: 冰川的过去仍留在土壤里，也留在每一道山谷的形状里。

examples.en: Glacial ice looks blue where it is compressed.
examples.cn: 冰川冰在受挤压处呈蓝色。

examples.en: The glacial period ended about ten thousand years ago.
examples.cn: 冰期在约一万年前结束。

examples.en: His glacial reply ended the conversation.
examples.cn: 他冷冰冰的回答结束了谈话。

dict_mnemonic.text: glaci（冰）+ -al（与……有关）：冰的、冰川的；温度引申为极冷与冷淡，速度引申为极慢，化学里则是像冰一样纯。

root: 拉丁 glacialis「冰的」，出 glacies「冰」；与 glacier、glaciation、glaciology 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of glacial. One adjective follows ice wherever it goes: into a glacier, into an ice age, into cold air, into a cold manner, into a slow pace, into chemistry and into the land ice carved.
sensesIntro.cn: glacial 的八个义项。同一个形容词跟着冰走遍各处：进冰川、进冰期、进冷空气、进冷淡态度、进缓慢速度、进化学，最后进入冰刻出的土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: blue-white ice pressed against stone, cold enough to make the air seem still.
core.cn: 核心意象：蓝白色的冰压在石头上，冷得让空气都像静止。

branches.en: THE WORK OF ICE: the glacier itself, the deposits it leaves, the valleys it cuts.
branches.cn: 冰的工作：冰川本身、留下的沉积、刻出的谷地。

branches.en: ICE AS TIME: a whole period named by its cover.
branches.cn: 冰作为时间：以冰盖命名的一整段时期。

branches.en: ICE AS TEMPERATURE: the literal cold of air and water.
branches.cn: 冰作为温度：空气与水的字面寒冷。

branches.en: ICE AS FEELING: a manner frozen toward other people.
branches.cn: 冰作为情感：对他人冻结的态度。

branches.en: ICE AS MEASURE AND APPEARANCE: the slowest pace, and an acid that looks like ice.
branches.cn: 冰作为尺度与外观：最慢的速度，以及看起来像冰的酸。

intro.en: Glacial is glaci- plus the Latin adjective suffix -alis, reduced to -al in English. It is the adjective member of the glacies family.
intro.cn: glacial 由 glaci- 加拉丁形容词后缀 -alis 构成，英语中缩为 -al。它是 glacies 词族的形容词成员。

latinIntro.en: Latin glacies yields the whole ice family: glacier, glacial, glaciate, glaciation, glaciology. All keep the sense of ice or freezing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 glacies 衍生整个冰词族：glacier、glacial、glaciate、glaciation、glaciology，全部保留冰或冻结之义。

items.example: Glacies covered the pond.
Glacialis aqua cut the throat.
Glacial, fluvial and rural share the pattern.
The glacier is thinning.

items.meaning: glacial cover or a glacial period
items.example: Glaciation left scattered boulders.
items.exampleCN: 冰川作用留下散落的巨砾。

items.example: The valley was glacially carved.
The last glacial period ended long ago.
items.exampleCN: 最后一次冰期早已结束。

items.meaning: concentrated acetic acid that looks like ice
items.example: Glacial acetic acid must be handled carefully.

definition_en: a mass of glacial ice covering a large area of land and spreading outward under its own weight
core_image: 一整块厚冰铺满大陆，边缘像糖浆一样向外缓慢摊开
scene: 飞机越过格陵兰上空，窗外是一整片没有尽头的白色，只有边缘露出黑色岩脊。Below them the ice sheet stretched to the horizon.
sceneCN: 这里 ice sheet 指「大陆冰盖」（第 1 个义项：覆盖大片陆地、靠自身重量向外流动的巨厚冰体）；句意为他们脚下的冰盖一直铺到天边。

pos.zh: 大陆冰盖；冰盖（可数，复数 ice sheets）

derivatives.zh: ice（复合词前项，古英语 īs，无后缀）→ 冰
ic-（ice 去 -e）+ -y（古英语 -ig，形容词后缀）→ 像冰一样的：结冰的、冰冷的
sheet（复合词后项，古英语 scēte，无后缀）→ 片；层；床单
ice + field（复合术语，无后缀）→ 连片冰区：冰原
ice + cap（复合术语，无后缀；cap 上溯晚期拉丁 cappa「头巾」）→ 覆于山顶或极区的穹状冰：冰帽
