senses.title: A continental ice mass
senses.titleCN: 大陆冰盖：覆盖大陆的巨厚冰体
senses.definition: a mass of ice covering a large land area and flowing outward under its own weight
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖大片陆地、靠自身重量向外流动的巨大冰体
senses.example: Below them the ice sheet stretched to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们脚下的冰盖一直铺到天边。
senses.why: sheet names a broad flat layer, and ice supplies the material; the compound is literally a sheet made of ice.
senses.whyCN: sheet 命名宽而平的层，ice 提供材料；这个复合词字面上就是「冰做的层」。

senses.title: The thickness and mass
senses.titleCN: 冰盖体量：厚度与质量
senses.definition: the body of ice considered as a volume with depth and mass
senses.definitionCN: 把冰体视为有厚度与质量的体积
senses.example: The ice sheet is almost three kilometres thick at its centre.
senses.exampleCN: 冰盖中心处厚近三公里。
senses.why: a sheet can be measured in thickness, so the word names a volume rather than only a surface.
senses.whyCN: 一层东西可以按厚度测量，因此这个词命名体积，而不只是表面。

senses.title: The area covered
senses.titleCN: 冰盖覆盖范围
senses.definition: the extent of land buried under the ice sheet
senses.definitionCN: 被冰盖掩埋的土地范围
senses.example: The ice sheet covers most of the island.
senses.exampleCN: 冰盖覆盖了该岛的大部分。
senses.why: the sheet also has a footprint, and geography names the land it buries.
senses.whyCN: 冰盖还有覆盖范围，地理学命名它所掩埋的土地。

senses.title: An ancient ice sheet
senses.titleCN: 古冰盖：更新世冰盖
senses.definition: an ice sheet of an earlier glaciation, known from deposits and landforms
senses.definitionCN: 更早冰期的冰盖，由沉积与地貌得知
senses.example: The Laurentide ice sheet once covered northern North America.
senses.exampleCN: 劳伦泰德冰盖曾经覆盖北美北部。
senses.why: past sheets are known from the deposits they left, so the word extends to ice that no longer exists.
senses.whyCN: 过去的冰盖由留下的沉积得知，因此这个词扩展到已不存在的冰。

senses.title: Mass balance and loss
senses.titleCN: 冰盖质量平衡与消融
senses.definition: the balance between snow added and ice lost through melting and calving
senses.definitionCN: 新增积雪与融化、崩解所失冰量之间的平衡
senses.example: The ice sheet loses mass faster than snow can replace it.
senses.exampleCN: 冰盖失去质量的速度快于积雪补充。
senses.why: a mass that gains snow and loses ice is treated as a budget, which is why mass balance is a standard phrase.
senses.whyCN: 既得雪又失冰的冰体被当作一份收支，因此 质量平衡（mass balance） 成为固定说法。

senses.title: The margin of the ice
senses.titleCN: 冰盖边缘与前缘
senses.definition: the outer edge where the ice sheet meets rock, sea or meltwater
senses.definitionCN: 冰盖与岩石、海洋或融水相接的外缘
senses.example: Meltwater ponds form along the ice sheet margin.
senses.exampleCN: 融水塘沿冰盖边缘形成。
senses.why: the margin is where ice meets rock, sea or melt, so the word names that boundary zone.
senses.whyCN: 边缘是冰与岩石、海或融水相接之处，因此这个词命名那条边界带。

senses.title: Ice as a climate archive
senses.titleCN: 冰盖作为气候档案
senses.definition: the ice sheet read as a record of past atmospheres in trapped air and layers
senses.definitionCN: 把冰盖读作封存空气与层序的古代大气记录
senses.example: Air bubbles in the ice sheet record ancient atmospheres.
senses.exampleCN: 冰盖中的气泡记录着古代大气。
senses.why: trapped air and annual layers make the ice a readable archive, so the word acquires a scientific sense as record.
senses.whyCN: 被封存的空气与年层使冰成为可读的档案，因此这个词获得「记录」的科学义。

senses.title: A polar cap on another planet
senses.titleCN: 行星科学：其他行星的极地冰盖
senses.definition: a large permanent ice deposit at the pole of another planet
senses.definitionCN: 另一颗行星极区的大型永久冰沉积
senses.example: Mars has ice sheets at both poles.
senses.exampleCN: 火星两极都有冰盖。
senses.why: the same morphology appears on Mars, so the term is extended beyond Earth.
senses.whyCN: 同样的形态在火星出现，因此这个术语被扩展到地球之外。

intro.en: Ice sheet is an English compound of ice and sheet. Ice goes back to Old English is, and sheet to Old English scete, a piece of cloth. The geological sense is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ice sheet 是英语复合词，由 ice 与 sheet 构成。ice 上承古英语 is，sheet 上承古英语 scete「一块布」。地质义是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Is is the Germanic word for ice, with German Eis and Dutch ijs as close relatives.
items.cn: is 是日耳曼语的冰词，德语 Eis 与荷兰语 ijs 是近亲。

items.en: Scete meant a piece of cloth or a corner, and later a broad flat layer of any material, such as a sheet of paper or metal.
items.cn: scete 指一块布或一角，后来指任何材料的宽平层，如一张纸或一块金属板。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geologists needed a term for ice that covers a continent rather than a valley, and borrowed the image of a sheet laid over the land.
items.cn: 19 世纪地质学家需要一个词指覆盖大陆而非山谷的冰，于是借用「铺在陆地上的层」这一意象。

items.en: By the twentieth century an ice sheet is defined technically: it covers more than fifty thousand square kilometres and spreads under its own weight.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，冰盖有了技术定义：面积超过五万平方公里，并靠自身重量向外摊开。

items.en: Ice sheet mass balance, ice cores and sea-level contribution become central measures in late twentieth-century climate research.
items.cn: 冰盖质量平衡、冰芯与对海平面的贡献成为 20 世纪后期气候研究的核心指标。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the two words are securely documented, but the compound's earliest citation is dated differently in different references.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：两个词均有可靠记载，但复合词的最早书证各家年代不一。

note.en: Group one holds the ice bodies that are constantly mistaken for one another; group two holds the wider terms of ice masses and ice movement.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互相认错的各类冰体；第二组是冰体与冰流的更宽术语。

entries.definition: A dome of ice over a summit or polar region, smaller than an ice sheet and not spreading over a continent.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖山顶或极地区域的穹状冰体，比冰盖小，也不铺满大陆。

entries.definition: A thick floating plate of ice attached to a coast; it is seaward of an ice sheet, not on land.
entries.definitionCN: 附着海岸、漂浮的厚冰板；它在冰盖靠海一侧，并不在陆地上。

entries.definition: A network of glaciers covering a mountain region, smaller and more broken than an ice sheet.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖山区的冰川网络，比冰盖小且更破碎。

entries.definition: Frozen seawater at the surface of the ocean; it floats and is not land ice.
entries.definitionCN: 海面冻结的海水；它漂浮着，并非陆地冰。

entries.definition: A body of ice confined by topography and flowing down a valley or out of an ice sheet.
entries.definitionCN: 受地形约束、沿谷下行或从冰盖流出的冰体。

entries.definition: Any large body of ice, used when size or type does not need to be specified.
entries.definitionCN: 任何大型冰体，用于无需指明大小或类型时。

entries.definition: A rapidly moving channel within an ice sheet, draining it like a river drains a basin.
entries.definitionCN: 冰盖内部快速流动的通道，像河流排干盆地一样排走冰。

entries.definition: Ice at either pole, whether on land or on sea; the term says where, not what shape.
entries.definitionCN: 两极的冰，无论在陆上还是海上；这个词说的是位置，而非形态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real neighbours, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与邻近术语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ice + sheet: a sheet of ice laid over a continent.
normal.cn: ice + sheet：铺在大陆上的一层冰。

normal.en: Size order: ice cap, ice field, ice sheet, with the sheet the largest and the cap the smallest.
normal.cn: 大小次序：冰帽、冰原、冰盖，冰盖最大，冰帽最小。

normal.en: An ice sheet rests on land; an ice shelf floats on sea. The second word tells you which.
normal.cn: 冰盖架在陆地上，冰架浮在海上；第二个词告诉你属于哪一种。

normal.en: Greenland and Antarctica each have one great ice sheet, which is why the names are fixed phrases.
normal.cn: 格陵兰与南极各有一块巨大冰盖，因此相关说法是固定短语。

normal.en: Ice sheet mass balance is income of snow minus loss of melt and calving.
normal.cn: 冰盖质量平衡就是积雪的收入减去融化与崩解的支出。

abstract.en: An ice sheet is a continent wearing its winter as a second skin.
abstract.cn: 冰盖是一块大陆把冬天当作第二层皮肤穿着。

abstract.en: An archive written in ice can be read only by melting it, which is the archive's danger.
abstract.cn: 以冰写成的档案只有融化才能读取，而这正是档案的危险。

abstract.en: Slow masses decide coastlines: an ice sheet can raise the sea without a single storm.
abstract.cn: 缓慢的巨物决定海岸线：一块冰盖不用一场风暴就能抬高海面。

examples.en: The Greenland ice sheet is losing mass every year.
examples.cn: 格陵兰冰盖每年都在失去质量。

examples.en: Scientists drill ice cores through the ice sheet.
examples.cn: 科学家钻透冰盖取冰芯。

examples.en: The ice sheet covered the continent during the last glaciation.
examples.cn: 上次冰期时冰盖覆盖了这片大陆。

dict_mnemonic.text: ice（冰）+ sheet（层、片）＝铺在大陆上的一层冰；比冰帽大、架在陆上、靠自身重量向外流，三个特征一起记。

root: 英语复合词，由 ice（冰，古英语 is）与 sheet（片、层，古英语 scete「一块布」）组合；地质义为 19 世纪所立。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of ice sheet. One continental body of ice produces the rest: its thickness, its area, its ancient forms, its balance, its edge, its record of air, and its counterparts on other planets.
sensesIntro.cn: ice sheet 的八个义项。一块大陆冰体衍生其余各义：厚度、面积、古代形态、质量平衡、边缘、封存的空气，以及其他行星上的对应物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick white layer spread over a whole continent, its edge slowly flowing outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：覆盖整块大陆的厚白层，边缘缓慢向外流动。

branches.en: THE BODY AND ITS FOOTPRINT: the ice mass, then the land it buries.
branches.cn: 冰体与其足迹：先是冰体，再是它掩埋的土地。

branches.en: MASS AND DEPTH: the same ice measured in kilometres.
branches.cn: 体量与厚度：以公里计的同一块冰。

branches.en: TIME AND BALANCE: an ancient sheet, then the accounting of gain and loss.
branches.cn: 时间与收支：先是一块古冰盖，再是增减的核算。

branches.en: EDGE AND ARCHIVE: where the ice meets the world, and what it keeps trapped inside.
branches.cn: 边缘与档案：冰与世界相接之处，以及它封存于内部的东西。

branches.en: ANOTHER PLANET: the same shape repeated at a Martian pole.
branches.cn: 另一颗行星：同一形状在火星极区重现。

intro.en: Ice sheet is a transparent compound of two free words, with no affix of its own; its technical force comes from the geological definition, not from morphology.
intro.cn: ice sheet 是两个自由词的透明复合，本身不带词缀；它的技术含义来自地质定义，而非构词。

latinIntro.en: Neither half has a Latin cognate: ice is Germanic and sheet is Germanic. Latin glacies also means ice, but it is a different root, not a relative; glacier and glacial belong to that other family.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都没有拉丁同族词：ice 与 sheet 都属日耳曼语。拉丁 glacies 也意为冰，但属另一词根，并非同源；glacier 与 glacial 属于那个词族。

items.example: Ice covered the bay.
A sheet of ice covered the lake.
The ice sheet is melting at its edges.
An ice cap covers the summit.

items.meaning: a mountain area of connected glaciers
items.meaningCN: 山区间相连冰川覆盖的区域
items.example: The ice field feeds many valleys.

items.meaning: a cylinder drilled from ice for study
items.meaningCN: 从冰中钻取用于研究的柱状样
items.example: The ice core records two thousand years.
items.exampleCN: 这根冰芯记录了两千年。

items.example: Ice sheets grew during the ice age.
The road was icy at dawn.

definition_zh: 冰帽；山顶冰盖；极地冰帽
definition_en: a dome of ice covering a mountain top or a polar region, smaller than an ice sheet
core_image: 一座圆顶山头被厚厚的冰整个罩住，像给山戴了一顶白帽子
scene: 远看那座火山，山顶被一层圆厚的冰罩住，边缘垂下一道道小冰川。An ice cap hides the summit for most of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 ice cap 指「冰帽」（第 1 个义项：覆盖山顶或极地区域、面积小于冰盖的穹状冰体）；句意为一年中大部分时间冰帽都遮住山顶。

pos.zh: 冰帽；山顶冰盖；极地冰帽（可数，复数 ice caps）

derivatives.zh: ice（复合词前项，古英语 īs，无后缀）→ 冰
ic-（ice 去 -e）+ -y（古英语 -ig，形容词后缀）→ 像冰一样的：结冰的、冰冷的
cap（复合词后项，晚期拉丁 cappa「头巾」，无后缀）→ 帽子；盖；顶
ice + cap 的连写形式（复合，无后缀改变）→ 冰帽
ice + cap + -ed（古英语过去分词后缀作形容词）→ 顶部覆冰的

senses.title: A summit ice cap
senses.titleCN: 山顶冰帽：罩住山头的穹状冰
senses.definition: a dome of ice covering the top of a mountain
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖山顶的穹状冰体
senses.example: An ice cap hides the summit for most of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 一年中大部分时间冰帽都遮住山顶。
senses.why: cap names a covering worn on top, so an ice cap is literally the ice a mountain wears on its head.
senses.whyCN: cap 命名戴在顶上的覆盖物，因此冰帽字面上就是山戴在头上的冰。

senses.title: A polar ice cap
senses.titleCN: 极地冰帽：极区海陆上的大冰盖
senses.definition: a large permanent cover of ice over a polar region, including sea ice in common usage
senses.definitionCN: 极区上方的大片永久冰盖，日常用法也含海冰
senses.example: The polar ice cap shrinks each September.
senses.exampleCN: 极地冰帽每年九月缩小。
senses.why: the same image scales up: a polar region is treated as a head wearing a cap of ice.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象放大：极区被当作戴着一顶冰帽的头。

senses.title: A small ice sheet in glaciology
senses.titleCN: 冰川学义：小于冰盖的穹状冰体
senses.definition: a dome-shaped mass of ice smaller than an ice sheet and not spreading over a continent
senses.definitionCN: 比冰盖小、不铺满大陆的穹状冰体
senses.example: Ice caps feed the valley glaciers below them.
senses.exampleCN: 冰帽供养着下方的山谷冰川。
senses.why: glaciology keeps the shape and adds a size limit, so cap becomes a technical category rather than a metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 冰川学保留形状并加上尺度限制，于是 cap 成为技术分类而非单纯比喻。

senses.title: The surface of an ice cap
senses.titleCN: 冰帽表面：可行走的冰穹顶
senses.definition: the upper surface of an ice cap, considered as terrain
senses.definitionCN: 冰帽的上表面，被视为一种地形
senses.example: Few plants survive on the ice cap.
senses.exampleCN: 冰帽上很少有植物存活。
senses.why: a dome has a surface you can walk on and map, so the word names terrain as well as ice.
senses.whyCN: 穹顶有可行走、可测绘的表面，因此这个词既命名冰，也命名地形。

senses.title: A Martian polar cap
senses.titleCN: 火星极冠：另一颗行星的极地冰
senses.definition: a permanent cap of water and carbon dioxide ice at the pole of Mars
senses.definitionCN: 火星极区由水冰与干冰构成的永久冰帽
senses.example: The Martian ice cap grows in winter and shrinks in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 火星极冠冬季扩大、夏季缩小。
senses.why: the same covering shape appears at the pole of Mars, so the term crosses planets.
senses.whyCN: 同样的覆盖形状出现在火星极区，因此这个术语跨越行星。

senses.title: The edge and meltwater
senses.titleCN: 冰帽边缘与融水径流
senses.definition: the margin of an ice cap, where meltwater leaves the ice
senses.definitionCN: 冰帽的边缘，融水由此离开冰体
senses.example: Streams run off the ice cap in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天溪流从冰帽流下。
senses.why: the edge is where melt leaves the ice, so the word names the margin and its runoff.
senses.whyCN: 边缘是融水离开冰体之处，因此这个词命名边缘及其径流。

senses.title: Ice cap retreat as a climate signal
senses.titleCN: 冰帽退缩作为气候信号
senses.definition: the shrinking of an ice cap, read as evidence of warming
senses.definitionCN: 冰帽缩小，被读作变暖的证据
senses.example: Warm summers thin the ice cap year by year.
senses.exampleCN: 温暖的夏天使冰帽逐年变薄。
senses.why: a shrinking cap is read as a measurement of warming, so the word becomes a climate indicator.
senses.whyCN: 缩小的冰帽被读作变暖的度量，因此这个词成为气候指标。

senses.title: A covering layer of ice
senses.titleCN: 比喻：顶部覆盖的一层冰
senses.definition: a thin or figurative layer of ice on top of something
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在某物顶部的一层薄冰或比喻性的冰层
senses.example: A cap of ice sealed the water butt.
senses.exampleCN: 一层冰封住了蓄水桶。
senses.why: anything wearing a thin frozen layer can be said to have a cap of ice, which is the literal image applied generally.
senses.whyCN: 任何覆着一层薄冰的东西都可以说有冰帽，这是字面意象的一般化。

intro.en: Ice cap joins ice, from Old English is, to cap, which came through Old English cæppe from Late Latin cappa 'hood'. The polar sense is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ice cap 把 ice（古英语 is）与 cap 并置，后者经古英语 cæppe 来自晚期拉丁 cappa「头巾」。极地义是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cappa named a hood or head-covering. Its own origin is uncertain; a link with Latin caput 'head' is often suggested but not demonstrated.
items.cn: cappa 指头巾或罩头之物。其自身来源不确定；与拉丁 caput「头」的联系常被提出，但未获证实。

items.en: Old English cæppe gave English cap, which extended from headgear to any covering lid, including the top of a bottle or a mountain.
items.cn: 古英语 cæppe 给出英语 cap，从头上戴的帽子扩展到任何覆盖用的盖子，包括瓶口与山顶。

items.en: Ice plus cap is a modern descriptive compound; nineteenth-century travellers and geologists used it for the ice covering polar lands and high summits.
items.cn: ice 加 cap 是近代的描述性复合词；19 世纪的旅行者与地质学家用它指覆盖极地与高峰的冰。

items.en: Twentieth-century glaciology distinguishes an ice cap from an ice sheet by size and by its domed, non-continental spread.
items.cn: 20 世纪冰川学按尺度与穹状、非大陆性的扩展方式，把冰帽与冰盖区分开。

items.en: Astronomers describe the seasonal caps at the poles of Mars as ice caps, extending the word beyond Earth.
items.cn: 天文学家把火星两极的季节性冰盖称作 ice caps，使这个词超出地球范围。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of cappa is disputed, and the compound's first date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代存疑）：cappa 的来源有争议，复合词的首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds the ice bodies most often confused with an ice cap; group two holds the words for domes and summits of ice.
note.cn: 第一组是最常与冰帽混淆的冰体；第二组是命名冰穹与山顶冰体的词。

entries.definition: A mass of ice covering a whole continent and spreading under its own weight; much larger than an ice cap.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖整块大陆并靠自重摊开的冰体；比冰帽大得多。

entries.definition: A floating ice plate attached to a coast; an ice cap rests on land or sea floor, not on water.
entries.definitionCN: 附着海岸的漂浮冰板；冰帽架在陆地或海底，而非浮在水上。

entries.definition: A network of valley glaciers covering a mountain region, more broken than a single dome.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖山区的谷冰川网络，比单个冰穹更破碎。

entries.definition: A covering of snow on a summit; it is seasonal and thin, not a mass of glacial ice.
entries.definitionCN: 山顶的积雪覆盖；它是季节性的薄层，不是冰川冰体。

entries.definition: The ice-covered region around a pole; the phrase stresses location rather than ice type.
entries.definitionCN: 极区周围覆冰的区域；这个说法强调位置，而非冰的类型。

entries.definition: A dome-shaped ice mass, the descriptive term behind the technical ice cap.
entries.definitionCN: 穹状冰体，是冰帽这一技术术语背后的描述性说法。

entries.definition: A glacier occupying a summit or cirque, which may or may not form a full cap.
entries.definitionCN: 占据山顶或冰斗的冰川，未必形成完整冰帽。

entries.definition: Granular snow in transition to glacial ice; it is the material of which a cap is built.
entries.definitionCN: 正在转变为冰川冰的粒状雪；它是构成冰帽的材料。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real neighbours, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与邻近术语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ice + cap: the ice a mountain wears on its head.
normal.cn: ice + cap：山戴在头上的那顶冰帽。

normal.en: An ice cap is domed and smaller; an ice sheet is flat and continental.
normal.cn: 冰帽穹顶状且较小，冰盖扁平且属大陆尺度。

normal.en: The polar ice cap can include sea ice in everyday speech, but glaciologists keep the technical term for land ice.
normal.cn: 日常说的极地冰帽可以包含海冰，但冰川学家把这一技术术语留给陆地冰。

normal.en: Mars has ice caps too, made of water ice and frozen carbon dioxide.
normal.cn: 火星也有冰帽，由水冰与干冰构成。

normal.en: Ice-capped is the adjective: an ice-capped volcano, an ice-capped continent.
normal.cn: ice-capped 是形容词：覆冰的火山、覆冰的大陆。

abstract.en: A cap can be taken off: an ice cap is the one hat a mountain cannot remove.
abstract.cn: 帽子可以摘下；冰帽却是山摘不掉的那一顶。

abstract.en: A small dome can decide the water supply of a whole plain below it.
abstract.cn: 一个小小冰穹能决定下方整片平原的供水。

abstract.en: Every summit wears its own weather, and the ice cap is that weather made solid.
abstract.cn: 每座山顶都戴着自己的天气，冰帽就是把那天气变成固体。

examples.en: The ice cap on the volcano is shrinking.
examples.cn: 火山上的冰帽正在缩小。

examples.en: Meltwater from the ice cap feeds the river below.
examples.cn: 冰帽融水供养下方的河流。

examples.en: The polar ice cap reached its yearly minimum in September.
examples.cn: 极地冰帽在九月达到年度最小值。

dict_mnemonic.text: ice（冰）+ cap（帽子）＝山或极区戴着的冰帽；穹状、较小、架在陆上，三点区分于冰盖。

root: 英语复合词，由 ice（冰，古英语 is）与 cap（帽、盖，经古英语 cæppe 上溯晚期拉丁 cappa「头巾」）组合。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of ice cap. A covering on a summit expands to a polar region, becomes a technical category in glaciology, acquires a Martian counterpart, and ends as any cap of ice.
sensesIntro.cn: ice cap 的八个义项。从山顶的覆盖物扩展到极区，成为冰川学的技术分类，再有了火星对应物，最后收束为任何一层冰盖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round white hat of ice sitting on top of a peak.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶圆白的冰帽扣在山顶。

branches.en: THE DOME AND ITS SURFACE: the cap on a peak, then the ground it offers.
branches.cn: 冰穹与其表面：先是山顶的帽，再是它提供的地面。

branches.en: THE POLAR SCALE: the same image applied to a whole polar region.
branches.cn: 极地尺度：同一意象放大到整个极区。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL CATEGORY: domed, smaller than a sheet, defined by glaciology.
branches.cn: 技术分类：穹状、小于冰盖，由冰川学界定。

branches.en: BEYOND EARTH AND AT THE EDGE: a Martian cap, then the meltwater leaving the margin.
branches.cn: 超越地球与边缘：先是火星极冠，再是从边缘流出的融水。

branches.en: SIGNAL AND METAPHOR: retreat as a climate measure, then any covering layer of ice.
branches.cn: 信号与比喻：退缩成为气候指标，再是任何覆盖的冰层。

intro.en: Ice cap is a plain compound. Cap contributes the image of a covering worn on top; ice contributes the material. Neither element carries an affix.
intro.cn: ice cap 是直接复合。cap 提供「戴在顶上的覆盖物」意象，ice 提供材料，两部分都不带词缀。

latinIntro.en: Cap descends from Late Latin cappa 'hood'; ice is Germanic with no Latin cognate. Latin glacies also means ice but belongs to a different root family.
latinIntro.cn: cap 上溯晚期拉丁 cappa「头巾」；ice 属日耳曼语，无拉丁同族词。拉丁 glacies 也意为冰，但属另一词根词族。

items.example: Ice sealed the summit.
A cap of snow covered the rock.

items.structure: cappa, cappae (f., first declension, Late Latin)
items.example: Cappa gave French chape and English cap.
items.exampleCN: cappa 给出法语 chape 与英语 cap。

items.example: The icecap is retreating.
An ice-capped peak rose above the plain.
items.exampleCN: 一座覆冰的山峰耸立在平原之上。

items.example: The polar cap expands in winter.

items.meaning: a hard layer over softer rock
items.meaningCN: 覆盖在软岩之上的硬岩层
items.example: Cap rock protects the plateau from erosion.
items.exampleCN: 盖岩保护高原免受侵蚀。

items.example: The wind capsized the small boat.

latinEntries.structure: cappa, cappae (f., first declension, Late Latin)

latinEntries.meaningCN: 头（与 cappa 的联系属推测）

definition_en: ground that remains frozen for two or more years, found in cold regions
core_image: 地面下几米深处一层硬得像石头的冻土，夏天地表化了，深处仍冻着
scene: 八月里地表已经化开一掌深，挖下去却碰到硬得像石头的冻层。The permafrost begins less than a metre below the moss.
sceneCN: 这里 permafrost 指「永久冻土」（第 1 个义项：连续两年以上保持冻结的地层）；句意为永冻层在苔藓下不到一米处就开始。

pos.zh: 永久冻土；永冻层（不可数，指多片冻土时偶作可数）

derivatives.zh: frost（复合词后项，古英语 forst，无后缀）→ 霜冻；使结霜
frost + -y（古英语 -ig，形容词后缀）→ 有霜的；引申为冷淡的
froz-（freeze 的过去分词词干）+ -en（古英语强变化过去分词后缀）→ 已冻结的
freez-（freeze）+ -ing（古英语 -ing，动名词与分词后缀）→ 结冰的过程；引申为极冷的、冰点
de-（拉丁否定与去除前缀）+ frost → 去除霜：除霜、解冻

senses.title: Ground frozen for years
senses.titleCN: 永久冻土：多年不化的地面
senses.definition: soil or rock that stays below freezing for at least two consecutive years
senses.definitionCN: 至少连续两年保持冰点以下温度的土壤或岩石
senses.example: The permafrost begins less than a metre below the moss.
senses.exampleCN: 永冻层在苔藓下不到一米处就开始。
senses.why: perma- is the clipped form of permanent and frost names frozen ground, so the word states its definition almost word for word.
senses.whyCN: perma- 是 permanent 的缩略，frost 指冻结的地面，因此这个词几乎逐字说出了自己的定义。

senses.title: The frozen layer as a geological unit
senses.titleCN: 永冻层：作为地质层位
senses.definition: the frozen layer considered as a distinct zone below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 被视为地表之下一个独立层位的冻结层
senses.example: The permafrost extends hundreds of metres down in Siberia.
senses.exampleCN: 在西伯利亚，永冻层向下延伸数百米。
senses.why: once a layer is mapped, the word names the zone itself rather than the property of being frozen.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这一层被测绘，这个词就命名该层位本身，而不只是「冻结」这一性质。

senses.title: The zone below the active layer
senses.titleCN: 活动层之下的冻层
senses.definition: the permanently frozen ground beneath the seasonally thawing active layer
senses.definitionCN: 季节性融化的活动层之下永久冻结的地面
senses.example: Above the permafrost lies an active layer that thaws each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 永冻层之上是每年夏天融化的活动层。
senses.why: the frozen layer is defined by contrast with the layer above it, so the word names a position in a vertical sequence.
senses.whyCN: 冻结层通过与上层对比而被界定，因此这个词命名垂直层序中的一个位置。

senses.title: Thawing permafrost
senses.titleCN: 冻土融化：气候变暖下的解冻
senses.definition: the process by which permafrost warms and thaws, often because of climate change
senses.definitionCN: 冻土升温并解冻的过程，常因气候变化而发生
senses.example: Thawing permafrost releases methane into the air.
senses.exampleCN: 融化的永久冻土把甲烷释放到空气中。
senses.why: the noun can name a process when the focus is on change rather than on the frozen state.
senses.whyCN: 当焦点在变化而非冻结状态时，这个名词可以命名一个过程。

senses.title: The permafrost zone as a region
senses.titleCN: 冻土带：以永冻层为特征的地区
senses.definition: a region where permafrost is widespread and shapes the landscape
senses.definitionCN: 永冻层广泛分布并塑造景观的地区
senses.example: Buildings in the permafrost zone need special foundations.
senses.exampleCN: 冻土带的建筑需要特殊地基。
senses.why: where the layer is continuous it characterises a whole region, so the word names a zone.
senses.whyCN: 在冻结层连续分布之处，它界定整个地区，因此这个词命名一个区域。

senses.title: A problem for engineering
senses.titleCN: 工程难题：冻土上的建设
senses.definition: the engineering challenge of building on ground that moves when it thaws
senses.definitionCN: 在解冻时会变形的地面上建造的工程难题
senses.example: The pipeline was designed to avoid melting the permafrost.
senses.exampleCN: 这条管道被设计成避免融化冻土。
senses.why: in engineering the word names not a material but a risk: frozen ground that loses strength when warmed.
senses.whyCN: 在工程语境中，这个词命名的不是材料，而是一种风险：受热就失去强度的冻土。

senses.title: Ancient permafrost as a preserver
senses.titleCN: 古冻土：封存遗骸的冻层
senses.definition: long-frozen ground that preserves organic remains for thousands of years
senses.definitionCN: 长期冻结、封存有机物遗骸数千年的地面
senses.example: Ancient permafrost preserved the mammoth's skin and hair.
senses.exampleCN: 古冻土保存了猛犸象的皮肤与毛发。
senses.why: cold and anoxic conditions stop decay, so the same ground becomes a preserver of ancient life.
senses.whyCN: 低温与缺氧阻止腐烂，因此同一地面成为古代生命的保存者。

senses.title: Frozen ground on other worlds
senses.titleCN: 行星科学：其他天体上的冻土
senses.definition: perennially frozen ground or ice-rich soil on another planet or moon
senses.definitionCN: 其他行星或卫星上常年冻结的地面或富冰土壤
senses.example: Orbiters look for permafrost beneath the Martian surface.
senses.exampleCN: 轨道器在火星表面之下寻找冻土。
senses.why: planetary scientists look for the same frozen layer elsewhere, so the term is extended beyond Earth.
senses.whyCN: 行星科学家在其他天体寻找同样的冻结层，因此这个术语被扩展到地球之外。

intro.en: Permafrost is a twentieth-century coinage: perma- is clipped from permanent, and frost goes back to Old English forst. The term is generally credited to the American geologist S. W. Muller in the 1940s. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: permafrost 是 20 世纪新造术语：perma- 由 permanent 缩略而来，frost 上承古英语 forst。一般认为该术语由美国地质学家西蒙·穆勒在 1940 年代提出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Forst meant frost or freezing, and is related to the verb freeze; it named both the event and the white deposit.
items.cn: forst 指霜冻或冻结，与动词 freeze 相关；它既指事件也指白色的霜。

items.en: Permanent comes from Latin permanens, the participle of permanere 'to remain throughout', built on per- 'through' and manere 'to stay'.
items.cn: permanent 来自拉丁 permanens，是 permanere「始终留存」的分词，由 per-「贯穿」与 manere「停留」构成。

items.en: S. W. Muller is generally credited with permafrost in 1943, in a study of frozen ground in Alaska; earlier Russian work used vechnaya merzlota 'eternal frost'.
items.cn: 一般认为西蒙·穆勒于 1943 年在阿拉斯加冻土研究中首创 permafrost；更早的俄国研究使用 vechnaya merzlota「永久冻土」。

items.en: After the Second World War the English term spread through cold-regions engineering and physical geography.
items.cn: 二战后，这个英语术语在寒区工程与自然地理学中传播开来。

items.en: From the late twentieth century, thawing permafrost enters climate science as a carbon source and as a threat to infrastructure.
items.cn: 从 20 世纪后期起，融化的冻土作为碳源与基础设施威胁进入气候科学。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and coinage): the attribution to Muller is conventional rather than certain, and earlier uses may exist.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与首创者存疑）：归功于穆勒属惯例说法而非确证，可能存在更早用法。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike or same-prefix words that are not frozen ground; group two holds the cold-ground vocabulary with which permafrost is confused.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或同前缀、却并非冻土的词；第二组是常与永久冻土混淆的寒冷地面词汇。

entries.definition: A design system for sustainable agriculture; its perma- is clipped from permanent, but it has nothing to do with frozen ground.
entries.definitionCN: 可持续农业的设计体系；其 perma- 也由 permanent 缩略，但与冻土无关。

entries.definition: Lasting without change; permafrost borrows its first element but adds the specific meaning of frozen ground.
entries.definitionCN: 持久不变的；permafrost 借用了它的第一成分，却加上冻土的具体含义。

entries.definition: Injury caused by freezing of body tissue; it shares frost but concerns bodies, not ground.
entries.definitionCN: 身体组织冻结造成的损伤；共享 frost，却关乎身体而非地面。

entries.definition: The upper surface of the permafrost layer, below the active layer.
entries.definitionCN: 永冻层的上表面，位于活动层之下。

entries.definition: The treeless cold region above or beyond the treeline; permafrost is the frozen ground beneath it.
entries.definitionCN: 树线以上或以外的无树寒冷地区；permafrost 是其下方的冻结地面。

entries.definition: Any ground below freezing, whether for one winter or for years; permafrost requires at least two.
entries.definitionCN: 任何冰点以下的地面，无论一个冬天还是多年；永冻土至少需两年。

entries.definition: The surface soil that thaws each summer above the permafrost.
entries.definitionCN: 每年夏天在永冻层之上融化的表层土壤。

entries.definition: Ice formed within soil or rock, which may or may not be part of permafrost.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤或岩石中形成的冰，未必属于永冻层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、同族词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: perma- (permanent) + frost: permanently frozen ground, the definition almost written into the word.
normal.cn: perma-（永久的）+ frost（冻）：永久冻结的地面，定义几乎写在词里。

normal.en: Two years is the threshold: one winter is frost, two years is permafrost.
normal.cn: 两年是门槛：一个冬天只是霜冻，连续两年才是永久冻土。

normal.en: The active layer thaws; the permafrost below does not.
normal.cn: 活动层会融化，下面的永冻层不会。

normal.en: Permafrost is both a material and a risk: solid when frozen, unstable when thawed.
normal.cn: 永久冻土既是材料也是风险：冻结时坚固，融化时不稳定。

normal.en: Permafrost, tundra and active layer form one vertical picture: frozen soil, its surface, and its seasonal skin.
normal.cn: 永久冻土、苔原与活动层构成一幅垂直图景：冻土、它的表面与季节性表层。

abstract.en: Permafrost is a freezer that no one switched on and no one can switch off.
abstract.cn: 永久冻土是一台没人打开、也没人能关掉的冰箱。

abstract.en: A thawing permafrost is an old debt being paid all at once.
abstract.cn: 融化的永久冻土是一笔被一次性偿还的旧账。

abstract.en: Buildings on permafrost are agreements with a ground that may change its mind.
abstract.cn: 建在永久冻土上的建筑，是与一块可能变卦的地面达成的协议。

examples.en: Permafrost underlies much of the Arctic.
examples.cn: 北极大部分地区底下是永久冻土。

examples.en: Thawing permafrost can damage roads and pipelines.
examples.cn: 融化的永久冻土会破坏道路与管道。

examples.en: Ancient permafrost preserved the animal's body for thousands of years.
examples.cn: 古冻土把这只动物的遗体保存了数千年。

dict_mnemonic.text: perma（永久）+ frost（冻）＝永久冻结的地面；记「两年门槛、活动层在上、融化即风险」三点。

root: 20 世纪新造术语，由 permanent 的缩略形式 perma- 与 frost（霜冻，古英语 forst）组合；一般认为由穆勒于 1943 年提出。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of permafrost. A definition becomes a layer, a zone, a process, an engineering risk, a preserver of ancient life and finally a feature sought on other worlds.
sensesIntro.cn: permafrost 的八个义项。一个定义先变成层位，再变成区域、过程、工程风险、古生物保存者，最后成为在其他天体上寻找的特征。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metre of soft moss above ground that is hard as stone below.
core.cn: 核心意象：地表一掌松软的苔藓之下，是硬得像石头的冻层。

branches.en: DEFINITION AND LAYER: frozen ground as a condition, then as a mapped unit.
branches.cn: 定义与层位：先是作为状态的冻土，再是作为测绘单元的冻层。

branches.en: THE VERTICAL STRUCTURE: what lies above and what lies below.
branches.cn: 垂直结构：上面是什么，下面是什么。

branches.en: THAW AND RELEASE: the process of melting, and the same search extended to other worlds.
branches.cn: 融化与释放：解冻过程，以及把同样的寻找扩展到其他天体。

branches.en: ZONE AND RISK: a region defined by frozen ground, and the engineering problem it creates.
branches.cn: 区域与风险：由冻土界定的地区，以及它造成的工程问题。

branches.en: THE OLD FREEZER: a preserver of bodies and organic matter across millennia.
branches.cn: 古老冰柜：跨越千年保存遗体与有机物。

intro.en: Permafrost is a blend-like coinage: a clipped combining form perma- plus the free noun frost. Neither element is an inherited English prefix.
intro.cn: permafrost 近似混成词：缩略组合形式 perma- 加自由名词 frost。两部分都不是英语继承下来的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Only perma- is Latin-derived, clipped from permanent, itself from Latin permanens and permanere. Frost is Germanic and has no Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 perma- 源自拉丁，由 permanent 缩略，而 permanent 出拉丁 permanens、permanere。frost 属日耳曼语，无拉丁同族词。

items.example: Permafrost and permaculture both use the clipped perma-.
items.exampleCN: permafrost 与 permaculture 都用缩略的 perma-。

items.example: Frost cracked the soil.
The mark is permanent.
The ground is permanently frozen.

items.meaning: covered with frost; cold in manner
items.example: A frosty morning hardened the mud.
items.exampleCN: 一个霜晨把泥地冻硬了。

items.example: The lake is frozen solid.
He defrosted the freezer.

items.meaning: the upper boundary of the frozen layer
items.example: The permafrost table lies below the active layer.
items.exampleCN: 冻土面位于活动层之下。

latinEntries.meaning: to remain throughout, stay to the end

definition_zh: 苔原；冻原；苔原带；（喻）荒凉地带
definition_en: a treeless cold region with low vegetation, found near the Arctic or above the treeline
core_image: 一眼望不到树的开阔地，地面是苔藓、地衣和矮灌木，风把云推得很低
scene: 夏天极昼，地面只有苔藓、地衣和矮柳，远处一头驯鹿慢慢走过。Reindeer graze across the open tundra in summer.
sceneCN: 这里 tundra 指「苔原」（第 1 个义项：极地或高山树线以上、无树的开阔寒冷地带）；句意为夏天驯鹿在这片开阔苔原上吃草。

pos.zh: 苔原；冻原；苔原带（可数，复数 tundras）

derivatives.zh: tundra + biome（复合术语，无后缀）→ 苔原生物群系
tundra + climate（复合术语，无后缀）→ 苔原气候
tundra + soil（复合术语，无后缀）→ 苔原土壤
tundra + vegetation（复合术语，无后缀）→ 苔原植被
tundra + zone（复合术语，无后缀）→ 苔原带

senses.title: The treeless Arctic plain
senses.titleCN: 极地苔原：无树的开阔寒冷地带
senses.definition: a treeless plain in a cold region, covered with moss, lichen and low shrubs
senses.definitionCN: 寒冷地区无树的平地，覆有苔藓、地衣与低矮灌木
senses.example: Reindeer graze across the open tundra in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天驯鹿在这片开阔苔原上吃草。
senses.why: tundra names a landscape defined by absence: no trees, a short season and ground that stays cold.
senses.whyCN: tundra 命名一种由「缺失」界定的景观：没有树、生长季短、地面长期寒冷。

senses.title: Alpine tundra above the treeline
senses.titleCN: 高山苔原：树线以上的无树地带
senses.definition: the treeless zone on a mountain above the local treeline
senses.definitionCN: 山地本地树线以上的无树地带
senses.example: Above the treeline lies a windswept alpine tundra.
senses.exampleCN: 树线之上是风大的高山苔原。
senses.why: altitude produces the same treeless cold conditions as latitude, so the word covers mountain zones too.
senses.whyCN: 高海拔与高纬度产生同样的无树寒冷条件，因此这个词也覆盖山地。

senses.title: Tundra vegetation
senses.titleCN: 苔原植被：苔藓、地衣与矮灌木
senses.definition: the plant community of mosses, lichens, grasses and dwarf shrubs
senses.definitionCN: 苔藓、地衣、禾草与矮灌木组成的植物群落
senses.example: Tundra vegetation grows only a few centimetres high.
senses.exampleCN: 苔原植被只长到几厘米高。
senses.why: the absence of trees leaves a low plant cover, and ecology names that cover as the tundra vegetation.
senses.whyCN: 树木缺失留下低矮植被，生态学把这层覆盖命名为苔原植被。

senses.title: Tundra soil and frozen subsoil
senses.titleCN: 苔原土壤与冻土环境
senses.definition: the thin, cold, often waterlogged soil above permafrost
senses.definitionCN: 永冻层之上薄、冷、常积水的土壤
senses.example: Tundra soil thaws only at the surface each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 苔原土壤每年夏天只在表层融化。
senses.why: the plants grow in a thin layer above frozen subsoil, so the word extends from landscape to soil.
senses.whyCN: 植物长在冻土之上的薄层里，因此这个词从景观延伸到土壤。

senses.title: The tundra as a biome
senses.titleCN: 苔原生物群系：环极的生物带
senses.definition: the circumpolar biome characterised by treeless vegetation and permafrost
senses.definitionCN: 以无树植被与永冻层为特征的环极生物群系
senses.example: The tundra biome circles the Arctic Ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 苔原生物群系环绕北冰洋。
senses.why: a landscape repeated around the pole becomes a biome, a unit of ecological classification.
senses.whyCN: 环绕极地重复出现的景观成为生物群系，即生态分类单位。

senses.title: The brief growing season
senses.titleCN: 苔原生长季：短暂的夏季花期
senses.definition: the short summer period when tundra plants flower and grow
senses.definitionCN: 苔原植物开花生长的短暂夏季
senses.example: The tundra blooms briefly in July.
senses.exampleCN: 苔原在七月短暂绽放。
senses.why: the short summer is the only window for growth, so the word also names that brief season.
senses.whyCN: 短暂的夏天是唯一的生长窗口，因此这个词也命名那段短季。

senses.title: A barren or empty field
senses.titleCN: 比喻：荒凉空旷的领域
senses.definition: any area or field seen as empty, cold and without growth
senses.definitionCN: 任何被视为空旷、寒冷、缺乏生长的领域
senses.example: Critics called the new district a cultural tundra.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把新区称为文化上的荒原。
senses.why: the metaphor transfers the absence of trees and life to culture, leaving an image of barren openness.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把「无树、少生命」的特征移到文化上，留下荒凉空旷的意象。

senses.title: Tundra climate
senses.titleCN: 苔原气候：冬季长而寒冷的气候型
senses.definition: a climate type with long cold winters and a short cool summer, supporting tundra
senses.definitionCN: 冬季漫长寒冷、夏季短暂凉爽、能维持苔原的气候类型
senses.example: Tundra climates have a month or two above freezing.
senses.exampleCN: 苔原气候只有一两个月高于冰点。
senses.why: the vegetation and frozen ground together imply a climate type, so the word extends to climate classification.
senses.whyCN: 植被与冻土共同蕴含一种气候型，因此这个词延伸到气候分类。

intro.en: Tundra was borrowed from Russian tundra, generally traced to Kildin Sami tundar 'treeless upland'; a Finnish source tunturi 'treeless hill' is also proposed. English took the word in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tundra 借自俄语 tundra，一般认为上溯基尔丁萨米语 tundar「无树高地」；也有芬兰语 tunturi「无树的山」一说。英语在 19 世纪借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Russian tundra named the treeless north of Siberia, and English travel writing adopted it in the 1840s.
items.cn: 俄语 tundra 指西伯利亚无树的北方，英语游记在 1840 年代吸收了它。

items.en: The Russian word is generally derived from Kildin Sami tundar, meaning a treeless upland or flat-topped hill.
items.cn: 一般认为俄语词来自基尔丁萨米语 tundar，意为无树的高地或平顶山。

items.en: Finnish tunturi 'treeless hill' is an alternative source; the two words belong to the wider Finnic and Sami stock, so both accounts may be partly right.
items.cn: 芬兰语 tunturi「无树的山」是另一来源说；两词同属更广的芬兰语与萨米语族，因此两种说法可能各有部分道理。

items.en: Nineteenth-century explorers and geographers extended the word from Siberian local use to the whole circumpolar belt.
items.cn: 19 世纪的探险家与地理学家把该词从西伯利亚地方用法扩展到整个环极地带。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology defines tundra by treeless vegetation, permafrost and a short growing season, separating it from taiga and steppe.
items.cn: 20 世纪生态学以无树植被、永冻层与短生长季界定苔原，把它与泰加林、草原区分开。

items.en: Source uncertain: the Sami and Finnish hypotheses coexist, and the exact borrowing path from Russian into English is not fully documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根来源存疑）：萨米语说与芬兰语说并存，从俄语进入英语的确切借入路径也没有完整记载。

note.en: Group one holds the cold-climate biome words that are constantly swapped; group two holds the plainer descriptions of barren ground.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换的寒带生物群系词；第二组是「荒芜地面」的朴素说法。

entries.definition: The northern coniferous forest belt south of the tundra; it has trees, which the tundra lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 苔原以南的北方针叶林带；它有树，而苔原没有。

entries.definition: A dry grassland of continental interiors, treeless but warm and grassy rather than frozen.
entries.definitionCN: 大陆内部的干旱草原，同样无树，但温暖多草而非冻结。

entries.definition: A tropical or subtropical grassland with scattered trees and a dry season.
entries.definitionCN: 热带或亚热带草原，散布树木并有旱季。

entries.definition: The vast treeless grassland of the South American lowlands, temperate rather than polar.
entries.definitionCN: 南美低地广阔的无树草原，属温带而非极地。

entries.definition: Land that supports little or no vegetation, without specifying cold or latitude.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎不长或完全不长植被的土地，未限定寒冷或纬度。

entries.definition: A cold desert of the polar regions, drier and even more barren than most tundra.
entries.definitionCN: 极区的寒冷荒漠，比多数苔原更干、更荒芜。

entries.definition: A grassy mountain zone above the treeline, greener and often lower than alpine tundra.
entries.definitionCN: 树线以上的草甸山地，比高山苔原更绿、通常更低。

entries.definition: An open, often peaty upland in temperate regions, treeless but not polar.
entries.definitionCN: 温带地区开阔、常含泥炭的高地，无树但不属极地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real relatives, real compounds and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的同族词、复合词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Tundra means no trees: if you see a forest, you have moved south into taiga.
normal.cn: 苔原就是没有树：看到森林，说明已南移到泰加林。

normal.en: Reindeer, moss, lichen and dwarf willow are the four pictures that belong to tundra.
normal.cn: 驯鹿、苔藓、地衣与矮柳是属于苔原的四幅画面。

normal.en: Alpine tundra is the mountain version; Arctic tundra is the polar version; the word is the same.
normal.cn: 高山苔原是山地版，北极苔原是极地版，用的是同一个词。

normal.en: Tundra soil sits above permafrost: thin on top, frozen below.
normal.cn: 苔原土壤坐在永冻层之上：上面薄，下面冻。

normal.en: The growing season lasts weeks, so tundra plants flower almost at once.
normal.cn: 生长季只有几周，因此苔原植物几乎同时开花。

abstract.en: A tundra is a place where the forest has been subtracted and only patience remains.
abstract.cn: 苔原是被抽走了森林、只剩耐心的地方。

abstract.en: Some institutions are tundras: open, cold, and unable to grow anything tall.
abstract.cn: 有些机构就是苔原：开阔、寒冷，长不出任何高大的东西。

abstract.en: The tundra keeps its history in the permafrost, not in the trees it never had.
abstract.cn: 苔原把历史保存在永冻层里，而不是它从未拥有的树木里。

examples.en: The tundra turns green for a few weeks each summer.
examples.cn: 苔原每年夏天有几周变绿。

examples.en: Polar bears roam the coastal tundra in search of seals.
examples.cn: 北极熊在沿海苔原上游荡寻找海豹。

examples.en: Few trees survive in the tundra because the subsoil stays frozen.
examples.cn: 苔原上很少有树存活，因为底土长期冻结。

dict_mnemonic.text: tundra 借自俄语，一般认为出萨米语「无树高地」：记苔藓、地衣、矮柳、驯鹿、冻土、短生长季这六件套。

root: 借自俄语 tundra，一般认为上溯基尔丁萨米语 tundar「无树高地」，另有芬兰语 tunturi「无树的山」一说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of tundra. A treeless landscape yields the alpine variant, the vegetation, the soil, the biome, the season, the metaphor and the climate type.
sensesIntro.cn: tundra 的八个义项。一种无树景观衍生出高山变体、植被、土壤、生物群系、生长季、比喻与气候型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open plain with no trees, a carpet of moss and lichen, and reindeer moving across it.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有树的开阔平地，苔藓与地衣铺成地毯，驯鹿在其上走过。

branches.en: TWO ALTITUDES: the polar plain, then the same zone on a mountain.
branches.cn: 两个高度：先是极地平地，再是山上的同一地带。

branches.en: WHAT GROWS AND WHAT IT GROWS IN: the low plants, then the thin frozen soil.
branches.cn: 长什么与长在什么上：先是低矮植物，再是薄而冻结的土壤。

branches.en: THE WHOLE AND THE CLIMATE: the biome as a belt, then the climate that sustains it.
branches.cn: 整体与气候：先是作为地带的生物群系，再是维持它的气候。

branches.en: THE SHORT SEASON: the brief summer when everything flowers at once.
branches.cn: 短暂季节：万物同时开花的短夏。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any open, cold and unproductive field.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何开阔、寒冷、缺乏产出的领域。

intro.en: Tundra is a borrowing with no English affix or compound structure; its apparent -a ending is part of the Russian noun, not a suffix.
intro.cn: tundra 是借词，没有英语词缀或复合结构；词尾的 -a 属于俄语名词本身，并非后缀。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin cognate: it comes from Russian and probably from Sami. Latin campus and terra describe open ground but are unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁同族词：它来自俄语，且很可能来自萨米语。拉丁 campus 与 terra 也描述开阔地面，但并无同源关系。

items.example: The tundra stretches to the coast.
The map marks the tundras of the north.
items.exampleCN: 地图标出北方的各片苔原。

items.meaning: the low plant cover of a tundra
items.example: Tundra vegetation recovers slowly.

items.meaning: the climate type of tundra regions
items.example: Tundra climate has a very short summer.
Tundra soil is poor in nutrients.
The tundra biome is fragile.
Alpine tundra covers the ridge.

items.meaning: the tundra of the far north
items.example: Arctic tundra thaws for two months.
items.exampleCN: 北极苔原每年解冻两个月。

definition_en: a place in a desert where water is found and plants grow
core_image: 沙海中央一小片棕榈和水的绿色圆斑，四周全是黄沙
scene: 驼队走了三天，地平线上出现一排棕榈和一片反光的水面。The caravan rested for two days at the oasis.
sceneCN: 这里 oasis 指「绿洲」（第 1 个义项：沙漠中有水源、能生长植物的地点）；句意为驼队在绿洲休息了两天。

pos.zh: 绿洲；安宁之地；慰藉（可数，希腊式复数 oases）

derivatives.zh: oasis 的希腊式复数（-es 来自希腊 -ες 经拉丁 -es，非派生后缀）→ 绿洲的复数
oasis + town（复合名词，无后缀）→ 建在绿洲上的城镇
oasis + agriculture（复合名词，无后缀）→ 依赖绿洲水源的农业
oasis + ecosystem（复合名词，无后缀）→ 绿洲生态系统
oasis + -like（古英语 -līc，表「像……」的形容词后缀）→ 绿洲般的

senses.title: A watered place in a desert
senses.titleCN: 沙漠绿洲：有水的绿色地点
senses.definition: a place in a desert where ground water reaches the surface and plants can grow
senses.definitionCN: 沙漠中地下水出露、植物得以生长的地方
senses.example: The caravan rested for two days at the oasis.
senses.exampleCN: 驼队在绿洲休息了两天。
senses.why: oasis names a spot defined by contrast: water and green in the middle of dry sand.
senses.whyCN: oasis 命名一个由对比界定的地点：干旱沙地中间的水与绿色。

senses.title: The water source itself
senses.titleCN: 绿洲水源：泉眼与地下水
senses.definition: the spring or well that supplies an oasis
senses.definitionCN: 供养绿洲的泉或井
senses.example: The oasis is fed by a spring that never dries.
senses.exampleCN: 这处绿洲由一眼永不干涸的泉供养。
senses.why: a green spot is made by water reaching the surface, so the word can name the spring that creates it.
senses.whyCN: 绿色地点由到达地表的水造就，因此这个词可以命名造就它的泉。

senses.title: An oasis settlement
senses.titleCN: 绿洲聚落：依水而建的村镇
senses.definition: a village or town built around an oasis
senses.definitionCN: 围绕绿洲建成的村庄或城镇
senses.example: A small oasis grew into a trading town.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小绿洲发展成了贸易城镇。
senses.why: water attracts people, and a settlement grows around the source, so the place-name extends to the village.
senses.whyCN: 水吸引人，聚落围绕水源生长，因此地点之名扩展到村庄。

senses.title: Oasis agriculture
senses.titleCN: 绿洲农业：依靠灌溉的耕作
senses.definition: farming practised on irrigated land within a desert oasis
senses.definitionCN: 在沙漠绿洲内依靠灌溉进行的耕作
senses.example: Oasis agriculture depends on careful water use.
senses.exampleCN: 绿洲农业依赖精打细算的用水。
senses.why: the same water supports irrigation, so the word names the farming system built on it.
senses.whyCN: 同样的水支撑灌溉，因此这个词命名建立在其上的农业体系。

senses.title: The oasis ecosystem
senses.titleCN: 绿洲生态系统：孤立而脆弱的生境
senses.definition: the community of palms, crops and animals supported by an oasis
senses.definitionCN: 由绿洲供养的棕榈、作物与动物群落
senses.example: The oasis ecosystem is isolated by surrounding desert.
senses.exampleCN: 绿洲生态系统被四周沙漠隔离。
senses.why: an isolated watered patch supports a distinct community, which ecology names as an ecosystem.
senses.whyCN: 孤立的有水斑块支撑独特群落，生态学称之为生态系统。

senses.title: A place of calm
senses.titleCN: 比喻：纷扰中的安宁之所
senses.definition: a quiet place or moment that feels protected from surrounding pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在周围压力中显得受保护的安静之处或时刻
senses.example: The library was an oasis of calm in the busy city.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆是繁忙城市中的一片宁静绿洲。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the contrast of dry and green: calm stands out because everything around it is demanding.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了「干旱与青绿」的对比：宁静之所以突出，因为四周都在索取。

senses.title: A small source of relief
senses.titleCN: 比喻：稀缺的慰藉与亮点
senses.definition: a small amount of something good in a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 困境中少量令人宽慰的好事
senses.example: The good news was an oasis in a week of failures.
senses.exampleCN: 那条好消息是一周失败中的一片绿洲。
senses.why: the contrast of dry and green is transferred from landscape to experience, giving a small good thing the name of a watered place.
senses.whyCN: 干旱与青绿的对比从景观移到经验，使一件小小的好事获得「有水之地」的名字。

senses.title: How an oasis forms
senses.titleCN: 绿洲形成：地下水出露的水文过程
senses.definition: the geological and hydrological process by which water reaches the desert surface
senses.definitionCN: 水到达沙漠表面的地质与水文过程
senses.example: The oasis forms where the aquifer meets a fault.
senses.exampleCN: 绿洲在含水层与断层相接处形成。
senses.why: hydrology asks how the water gets there, so the word also names the process of formation.
senses.whyCN: 水文学追问水如何到达那里，因此这个词也命名形成过程。

intro.en: Oasis came into English through Latin and Greek from an Egyptian word for a watered place in the desert, probably Coptic ouahe. English has used it since the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oasis 经拉丁语与希腊语进入英语，源头是埃及语中指沙漠中水源地的词，可能是科普特语 ouahe。英语自 17 世纪使用。年代均为约数。

items.en: An Egyptian word, transliterated roughly as wahat, named a fertile spot in the desert; the exact vocalisation is reconstructed.
items.cn: 一个埃及语词，转写大致作 wahat，指沙漠中的肥沃地点；确切元音属重构。

items.en: Greek writers used oasis for the watered depressions of the Libyan desert, and the Greek form is the one that reached Europe.
items.cn: 希腊作者用 oasis 指利比亚沙漠中有水的洼地，进入欧洲的正是这个希腊形式。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun unchanged; English took it from Latin or French in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入这个希腊名词；英语在 17 世纪从拉丁语或法语借入。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century exploration fixed the modern image of palm trees, a pool and a caravan.
items.cn: 18 与 19 世纪的探险固定了棕榈、水塘与驼队的现代意象。

items.en: By the twentieth century an oasis can be any small area of calm or relief inside a hostile surroundings.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，绿洲可以指敌意环境中的任何一小片安宁或慰藉。

items.en: Source uncertain: the Egyptian-to-Greek transmission and the exact vocalisation are reconstructed, and the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代存疑）：从埃及语到希腊语的传递与确切元音形式属重构，英语首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds the plural and the look-alikes most often confused with oasis; group two holds the words for watered places and refuges.
note.cn: 第一组是复数形式与最易混淆的形近词；第二组是「有水之处」与「庇护所」的说法。

entries.definition: The plural of oasis, not a separate place; English keeps the Greek -es ending.
entries.definitionCN: oasis 的复数，并非另一个地点；英语保留希腊语 -es 词尾。

entries.definition: An imaginary line about which a body turns; it is shorter and differently stressed.
entries.definitionCN: 物体绕其旋转的假想线；词更短，重音也不同。

entries.definition: A suffix meaning a condition or process, as in osmosis or diagnosis; it is not a noun for a place.
entries.definitionCN: 表示状态或过程的后缀，如 osmosis、diagnosis；它不是地点的名词。

entries.definition: A brand or band name borrowed from the common noun; in such uses it no longer means a watered place.
entries.definitionCN: 借自普通名词的品牌或乐队名；这类用法不再指有水之地。

entries.definition: A natural pool where animals drink, usually smaller and less planted than an oasis.
entries.definitionCN: 动物饮水的天然水塘，通常比绿洲小、植被少。

entries.definition: A place where ground water flows naturally to the surface; an oasis may be built around one.
entries.definitionCN: 地下水自然流出地表之处；绿洲可能围绕泉形成。

entries.definition: A place of safety or rest; the metaphorical oasis is a haven of calm.
entries.definitionCN: 安全或休憩之处；比喻的绿洲就是宁静的避风港。

entries.definition: A place that shelters someone from danger or trouble, closer to the oasis metaphor than to its geography.
entries.definitionCN: 使人免受危险或困扰的庇护处，更接近绿洲的比喻而非地理义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real plurals, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复数形式、同族词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One oasis, two oases: the Greek plural keeps -es, unlike the English -s.
normal.cn: 一个 oasis，两个 oases：希腊式复数保留 -es，而非英语的 -s。

normal.en: Oasis is green surrounded by dry: the word is built on contrast.
normal.cn: 绿洲是被干旱包围的绿：这个词建立在对比之上。

normal.en: An oasis has three parts: water, palms and people.
normal.cn: 绿洲有三部分：水、棕榈与人。

normal.en: An oasis of calm and an oasis of good news use the same contrast, with no sand.
normal.cn: 「宁静绿洲」与「好消息绿洲」用的是同一种对比，只是没有沙。

normal.en: In hydrology an oasis marks where an aquifer meets the surface.
normal.cn: 在水文学中，绿洲标记含水层与地表相接之处。

abstract.en: An oasis is a small argument against the desert.
abstract.cn: 绿洲是对沙漠的一个小小反驳。

abstract.en: Every long journey needs one oasis, even if it is only a hour of sleep.
abstract.cn: 每段长途都需要一片绿洲，哪怕只是一小时睡眠。

abstract.en: Kindness in a harsh week is an oasis: small, watered, and remembered.
abstract.cn: 艰难一周里的善意就是绿洲：不大、有水，且被记住。

examples.en: The oasis supports date palms and a small village.
examples.cn: 这片绿洲供养着枣椰树和一个小村庄。

examples.en: They found an oasis after three days in the desert.
examples.cn: 在沙漠里走了三天后，他们找到一片绿洲。

examples.en: The reading room was an oasis of quiet.
examples.cn: 阅览室是一片安静的绿洲。

dict_mnemonic.text: oasis＝沙漠里的一小片水与绿；复数 oases 用希腊式；引申为「纷扰中的安宁」与「困境中的慰藉」。

root: 经拉丁 oasis 与希腊 oasis 上溯埃及语中指沙漠水源地的词（可能为科普特语 ouahe）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of oasis. Water in dry land generates the spring, the settlement, the farming, the ecosystem, the hydrological origin, and then two metaphors of relief.
sensesIntro.cn: oasis 的八个义项。干旱之地中的水衍生出泉源、聚落、农业、生态系统与水文成因，再衍生出两种「宽慰」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small green circle of palms and water in the middle of yellow sand.
core.cn: 核心意象：黄沙中央一小圈棕榈与水的绿色。

branches.en: THE PLACE AND ITS WATER: the green spot, then the spring that makes it.
branches.cn: 地点与水：先是绿色地点，再是造就它的泉。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND CROPS: the settlement built there, then the farming it supports.
branches.cn: 人与作物：先是在那里建起的聚落，再是它支撑的农业。

branches.en: THE ECOSYSTEM: an isolated community of plants and animals.
branches.cn: 生态系统：孤立的动植物群落。

branches.en: TWO METAPHORS OF RELIEF: calm inside noise, and good news inside failure.
branches.cn: 两种宽慰隐喻：喧闹中的安宁，失败中的好消息。

branches.en: THE HYDROLOGICAL ORIGIN: how water reaches the surface at all.
branches.cn: 水文成因：水究竟如何到达地表。

intro.en: Oasis is a borrowed noun with no English affix; its plural oases is the Greek pattern, and its productive life is in compounds such as oasis town.
intro.cn: oasis 是借入名词，不带英语词缀；复数 oases 是希腊式变化，它的构词活力体现在 oasis town 这类复合词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin oasis is itself a borrowing from Greek, which took it from Egyptian; there is no Latin root family to trace. Latin aqua and fons mean water and spring but are unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 oasis 本身借自希腊语，希腊语又借自埃及语，因此没有可追溯的拉丁词根词族。拉丁 aqua 与 fons 意为水与泉，但并不同源。

items.meaning: a watered place in a desert
items.example: The oasis lies halfway across the sand.
Three oases dot the route.
items.exampleCN: 路线上散布着三片绿洲。

items.meaning: a town built at an oasis
items.example: The oasis town trades in dates.
items.exampleCN: 这座绿洲城镇做枣椰贸易。

items.meaning: irrigated farming in a desert oasis
items.meaningCN: 沙漠绿洲中的灌溉农业
items.example: Oasis agriculture uses drip irrigation.

items.meaning: the living community of an oasis
items.example: The oasis ecosystem includes migratory birds.
items.exampleCN: 绿洲生态系统包括候鸟。

items.example: The garden is an oasis of calm.
items.exampleCN: 这座花园是一片宁静的绿洲。

items.meaning: the cooling and moistening influence of a watered patch on its surroundings
items.meaningCN: 有水的斑块对周围环境的降温增湿作用
items.example: The oasis effect lowers local temperatures.
items.exampleCN: 绿洲效应降低局部温度。

items.example: A few oasis-like patches survive the drought.
items.exampleCN: 少数像绿洲一样的斑块熬过了干旱。

latinEntries.structure: oasis, oasis (f., third declension, from Greek)
latinEntries.meaning: a watered place in the desert

definition_en: a hill of sand piled up by the wind
core_image: 风把沙一层层推上坡，脊线像刀刃，背风面陡下去
scene: 海边的风把细沙堆成一道弯月形的坡，脊线在夕阳下像刀刃。Wind pushed loose sand into a crescent dune behind the beach.
sceneCN: 这里 dune 指「沙丘」（第 1 个义项：风把沙堆积成的丘状地形）；句意为风把松散的沙堆成海滩后方的一道新月形沙丘。

pos.zh: 沙丘；沙丘状堆积（可数，复数 dunes）

forms.label: 形容词（沙丘的，技术用语）

derivatives.zh: dun-（dune 去 -e）+ -al（拉丁 -alis，表「与……有关的」）→ 沙丘的（地貌学术语）
dune + field（复合术语，无后缀）→ 成片沙丘：沙丘群、沙丘原
dune + ridge（复合术语，无后缀）→ 沙丘的脊线：沙丘脊
sand + dune（复合名词，无后缀）→ 由沙堆成的沙丘
dune + buggy（复合名词，无后缀）→ 在沙丘上行驶的越野车

senses.title: A wind-built hill of sand
senses.titleCN: 风成沙丘：风堆起的沙丘
senses.definition: a mound or ridge of sand built by wind
senses.definitionCN: 由风堆积而成的沙丘或沙脊
senses.example: Wind pushed loose sand into a crescent dune behind the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 风把松散的沙堆成海滩后方的一道新月形沙丘。
senses.why: dune names the shape wind makes when it runs out of strength and drops its load.
senses.whyCN: dune 命名风在失去力量、卸下负荷时造出的形状。

senses.title: A coastal dune
senses.titleCN: 海岸沙丘：海滩后方的沙丘带
senses.definition: a sand hill formed behind a beach by onshore wind
senses.definitionCN: 由向岸风在海滩后方形成的沙丘
senses.example: Marram grass holds the coastal dune together.
senses.exampleCN: 滨草把海岸沙丘固定在一起。
senses.why: coastal dunes are built by the same wind mechanism, with vegetation added, so the word covers the coastal case.
senses.whyCN: 海岸沙丘由同样的风的机制造成，只是多了植被，因此这个词覆盖海岸情形。

senses.title: A dune field
senses.titleCN: 沙丘群：成片分布的沙丘
senses.definition: a broad area covered by many dunes
senses.definitionCN: 被众多沙丘覆盖的广阔区域
senses.example: The dune field stretches for thirty kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沙丘群绵延三十公里。
senses.why: dunes rarely stand alone; a field of them is the normal landscape unit, so the word extends to the group.
senses.whyCN: 沙丘很少单独存在；成片的沙丘才是常见景观单元，因此这个词扩展到沙丘群。

senses.title: A dune type
senses.titleCN: 沙丘类型：新月形、线形与星形
senses.definition: one of the classified shapes of dunes, set by wind direction and sand supply
senses.definitionCN: 按风向与供沙量划分的沙丘形态类别
senses.example: Star dunes form where winds blow from several directions.
senses.exampleCN: 星形沙丘在多个方向来风处形成。
senses.why: wind direction and sand supply produce repeatable shapes, so the word names classes rather than single hills.
senses.whyCN: 风向与供沙量产生可重复的形状，因此这个词命名类别而非单个沙丘。

senses.title: Dune migration
senses.titleCN: 沙丘迁移：整体向下风移动
senses.definition: the slow movement of a dune as sand is moved from one face to the other
senses.definitionCN: 沙从一面移到另一面、导致沙丘整体向下风缓慢移动
senses.example: The dune advances several metres each year.
senses.exampleCN: 这座沙丘每年向前推进数米。
senses.why: sand moves across the crest, so the whole dune advances and the word names that motion.
senses.whyCN: 沙越过脊线移动，整座沙丘因此前移，这个词命名这种运动。

senses.title: The surface and crest
senses.titleCN: 沙丘表面与脊线
senses.definition: the rippled surface and sharp crest of a dune
senses.definitionCN: 沙丘有沙纹的表面与锋利的脊线
senses.example: Ripples cover the windward face of the dune.
senses.exampleCN: 沙丘的迎风面布满沙纹。
senses.why: the surface records the same wind at a smaller scale, so the word names ripples and crest as well as the hill.
senses.whyCN: 表面在更小尺度上记录同样的风，因此这个词既命名沙丘，也命名沙纹与脊线。

senses.title: Dune vegetation and stability
senses.titleCN: 沙丘植被与固沙
senses.definition: the plants that colonise and stabilise a dune
senses.definitionCN: 在沙丘上定居并固定沙丘的植物
senses.example: Dune vegetation traps sand and builds soil.
senses.exampleCN: 沙丘植被拦沙并积累土壤。
senses.why: plants colonise and hold the sand, so the word names the biological process that stabilises a dune.
senses.whyCN: 植物定居并固定沙，因此这个词命名稳定沙丘的生物过程。

senses.title: A mound of loose material
senses.titleCN: 比喻：堆积成丘之物
senses.definition: any mound of loose material piled by wind or another force
senses.definitionCN: 任何由风或其他力量堆成的松散物小丘
senses.example: A dune of snow blocked the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆雪丘堵住了大门。
senses.why: the shape is not limited to sand, so any wind-piled mound can take the name.
senses.whyCN: 这种形状并不限于沙，因此任何风堆成的小丘都可以用这个名字。

intro.en: Dune came into English from French dune, from Middle Dutch dune, the ancestor of modern Dutch duin. English adopted it in the late eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dune 经法语 dune 来自中古荷兰语 dune，是现代荷兰语 duin 的前身。英语在 18 世纪后期吸收。年代均为约数。

items.en: Middle Dutch dune named the sand hills of the coast; modern Dutch still has duin.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 dune 指海岸沙丘；现代荷兰语仍作 duin。

items.en: French borrowed the Dutch word for the sand hills of the North Sea coast, and English took it from French around the 1790s.
items.cn: 法语借入这个荷兰词，指北海沿岸沙丘；英语约在 1790 年代从法语借入。

items.en: The word goes back to a Germanic root for a hill or mound; English down, as in the South Downs, is generally considered a cognate.
items.cn: 该词上溯日耳曼语中表示丘或土堆的词根；英语 down（如 South Downs）一般被认为是同源词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geographers classify dune ridges, blowouts and migrating dune fields.
items.cn: 19 世纪地理学家对沙丘脊、风蚀坑与迁移沙丘群进行分类。

items.en: Twentieth-century conservation treats dunes as fragile habitats requiring stabilization and managed access.
items.cn: 20 世纪保护工作把沙丘视为需要固沙与限制进入的脆弱生境。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper Germanic root is reconstructed, and the exact first English date varies by a few years.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代存疑）：更早的日耳曼词根属重构，英语确切首见年代各家相差数年。

note.en: Group one holds the short words most often mistaken for dune; group two holds the landforms that resemble a dune without being one.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易被误认成 dune 的短词；第二组是形似沙丘却并非沙丘的地形。

entries.definition: A chalk upland in names such as the South Downs, or the everyday adverb; it is a cognate of dune but not a dune.
entries.definitionCN: 在 South Downs 这类地名中指白垩高地，或日常副词；与 dune 同源，但并非沙丘。

entries.definition: A dull grey-brown colour, or to demand payment; it is a different word with a shorter vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 暗灰褐色，或催讨款项；这是另一个词，元音更短。

entries.definition: More than one dune; the -s adds number only.
entries.definitionCN: 不止一座沙丘；-s 只增加数。

entries.definition: Of or relating to dunes, as in dunal vegetation or a dunal ridge.
entries.definitionCN: 沙丘的、与沙丘有关的，如沙丘植被或沙丘脊。

entries.definition: A rounded heap of earth or stones, not necessarily made of sand or by wind.
entries.definitionCN: 土石堆成的圆丘，未必由沙构成或由风造成。

entries.definition: A long narrow raised line, which may be the crest of a dune or a mountain.
entries.definitionCN: 狭长的隆起线，可以是沙丘脊，也可以是山脊。

entries.definition: A raised strip of ground, often beside water; a dune is a bank of dry sand.
entries.definitionCN: 隆起的土带，常在水边；沙丘是干沙构成的土埂。

entries.definition: Loose material, especially snow, piled by wind; a snow drift is a dune of snow.
entries.definitionCN: 被风堆起的松散物，尤指雪；雪堆就是雪的沙丘。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real cognates, real compounds and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的同源词、复合词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dune and down are cognates: both are Germanic words for a hill, but only dune is sand.
normal.cn: dune 与 down 同源：都是日耳曼语的「丘」，但只有 dune 是沙。

normal.en: A dune has a gentle windward face and a steep leeward face; the difference is the whole mechanism.
normal.cn: 沙丘迎风面平缓、背风面陡峭；这个差别就是全部机制。

normal.en: Dune migration is sand moving from the windward face over the crest to the leeward face.
normal.cn: 沙丘迁移就是沙从迎风面越过脊线落到背风面。

normal.en: Marram grass is the classic dune stabiliser on European coasts.
normal.cn: 滨草是欧洲海岸最典型的固沙植物。

normal.en: Sand dune, dune field and dune ridge all keep dune as the first or second element.
normal.cn: sand dune、dune field、dune ridge 都以 dune 为构词成分。

abstract.en: A dune is a wave of sand that takes years to break.
abstract.cn: 沙丘是一道要花多年才破碎的沙浪。

abstract.en: Anything loose will pile up somewhere; a dune is where the wind admits it has dropped something.
abstract.cn: 松散之物总会堆到某处；沙丘就是风承认自己卸下东西的地方。

abstract.en: A dune looks permanent and is the most temporary thing in the landscape.
abstract.cn: 沙丘看似永久，却是景观中最短暂的东西。

examples.en: The dune shifted two metres during the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴期间沙丘移动了两米。

examples.en: They climbed the steep face of the dune.
examples.cn: 他们爬上沙丘陡峭的一面。

examples.en: Grass was planted to keep the dune from moving.
examples.cn: 人们种草以防止沙丘移动。

dict_mnemonic.text: dune＝风堆起的一道沙丘；记「缓迎风、陡背风、会迁移」三特征，再记它借自荷兰语 duin。

root: 经法语 dune 来自中古荷兰语 dune（现代 duin），上溯日耳曼语表示「丘」的词根；与英语 down 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of dune. A wind-built hill yields coastal forms, fields of dunes, classified shapes, migration, surface detail, vegetation, and finally any mound of loose material.
sensesIntro.cn: dune 的八个义项。风成的丘衍生出海岸沙丘、沙丘群、形态分类、迁移、表面细节、植被，最后是任何松散物堆成的小丘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wind pushes sand up a gentle slope until it spills over a sharp crest.
core.cn: 核心意象：风把沙推上缓坡，直到沙越过锋利脊线倾泻下去。

branches.en: SINGLE HILLS: a wind-built mound, then the coastal version held by grass.
branches.cn: 单个沙丘：先是风成土丘，再是被草固定的海岸沙丘。

branches.en: FIELDS AND TYPES: many dunes together, then their classified shapes.
branches.cn: 沙丘群与类型：先是众多沙丘并存，再是形态分类。

branches.en: MOTION: the whole dune advancing as sand crosses the crest.
branches.cn: 运动：沙越过脊线，整座沙丘前移。

branches.en: SURFACE AND LIFE: ripples on the face, then the plants that trap sand.
branches.cn: 表面与生命：先是坡面沙纹，再是拦沙的植物。

branches.en: THE GENERAL MOUND: any loose material piled by wind or another force.
branches.cn: 一般化的小丘：任何由风或其他力量堆起的松散物。

intro.en: Dune is a bare borrowed noun; English adds only the learned adjective dunal and the ordinary plural -s.
intro.cn: dune 是光裸的借入名词；英语只添加学术形容词 dunal 与普通复数 -s。

latinIntro.en: Dune has no Latin cognate: it is Germanic through Dutch and French. Latin tumulus means a mound but is unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: dune 没有拉丁同族词：它经荷兰语与法语来自日耳曼语。拉丁 tumulus 意为土丘，但并不同源。

items.example: The dune rises above the beach.
The dunes run along the coast.
Dunal plants tolerate salt and wind.
The snow formed dune-like shapes.
items.exampleCN: 雪形成像沙丘一样的形状。

items.example: The dune field blocks the road each spring.
items.exampleCN: 每年春天沙丘群都会阻断道路。

items.example: A dune ridge runs parallel to the shore.
items.exampleCN: 一道沙丘脊与海岸平行。

items.meaning: a dune, with the material named first
items.meaningCN: 以材料在前构成的沙丘说法
items.example: Sand dunes protect the hinterland from waves.
items.exampleCN: 沙丘保护内陆免受海浪侵袭。

items.example: They drove a dune buggy along the shore.
items.exampleCN: 他们开沙丘越野车沿海岸行驶。

definition_en: a strong wind that carries sand and dust through the air
core_image: 一堵黄褐色的沙墙从地平线推过来，把天空和太阳一起吞掉
scene: 午后远处地平线升起一堵黄褐色的墙，几分钟内把太阳吞掉。A sandstorm turned noon into dusk and forced the convoy to stop.
sceneCN: 这里 sandstorm 指「沙尘暴」（第 1 个义项：强风把大量沙尘卷起、遮蔽天空的天气现象）；句意为沙尘暴把正午变成黄昏，车队被迫停下。

pos.zh: 沙尘暴；沙暴（可数，复数 sandstorms）

derivatives.zh: sand（复合词前项，古英语 sand，无后缀）→ 沙
sand + -y（古英语 -ig，形容词后缀）→ 多沙的；引申为沙色的
storm（复合词后项，古英语 storm，无后缀）→ 风暴；暴风雨
storm + -y（古英语 -ig，形容词后缀）→ 有风暴的；引申为激烈的
dust + storm（复合术语，无后缀）→ 以细尘为主的风暴：尘暴

senses.title: A wind-borne wall of sand
senses.titleCN: 沙尘暴：强风卷沙蔽空
senses.definition: a strong wind carrying large amounts of sand and dust, reducing visibility
senses.definitionCN: 强风携带大量沙尘、降低能见度的天气现象
senses.example: A sandstorm turned noon into dusk and forced the convoy to stop.
senses.exampleCN: 沙尘暴把正午变成黄昏，车队被迫停下。
senses.why: sand and storm are placed side by side: the word names a storm whose visible load is sand.
senses.whyCN: sand 与 storm 直接并置：这个词命名一场可见负荷为沙的风暴。

senses.title: A sand-dominated wind
senses.titleCN: 沙暴：以沙粒为主的强风
senses.definition: a wind event dominated by coarse sand rather than fine dust
senses.definitionCN: 以粗沙粒而非细尘为主的强风事件
senses.example: The sandstorm stripped paint from the cars.
senses.exampleCN: 沙暴把车漆打磨掉了。
senses.why: meteorology separates coarse sand from fine dust, so the same event has a sand-dominated reading.
senses.whyCN: 气象学把粗沙与细尘分开，因此同一事件有「以沙为主」的读法。

senses.title: The sand and dust it leaves
senses.titleCN: 落尘：沙尘暴留下的沙土
senses.definition: the sand and dust deposited after a sandstorm passes
senses.definitionCN: 沙尘暴过后落下的沙与尘
senses.example: The sandstorm left a layer of dust on every window.
senses.exampleCN: 沙尘暴在每扇窗上留下一层尘土。
senses.why: the storm deposits what it carries, so the word names the material left behind as well as the event.
senses.whyCN: 风暴卸下它所携带之物，因此这个词既命名事件，也命名留下的材料。

senses.title: A single storm event
senses.titleCN: 一次沙暴事件：可计数的一场
senses.definition: one occurrence of such a storm, countable in weather records
senses.definitionCN: 此类风暴的一次发生，在气象记录中可计数
senses.example: The region records dozens of sandstorms a year.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区每年记录数十次沙尘暴。
senses.why: weather records count events, so the mass noun acquires a countable sense.
senses.whyCN: 气象记录要计数事件，因此这个物质名词获得可数义。

senses.title: A sand source area
senses.titleCN: 沙源地：沙尘暴的物质来源
senses.definition: a dry area, such as a lake bed or desert, that supplies sand to storms
senses.definitionCN: 干涸湖床或沙漠等向风暴提供沙尘的地区
senses.example: Dry lake beds are major sandstorm sources.
senses.exampleCN: 干涸湖床是主要的沙尘暴源地。
senses.why: every storm starts somewhere dry, so the word names the source area as well as the event.
senses.whyCN: 每场沙尘暴都起于某处干旱地面，因此这个词既命名事件，也命名源地。

senses.title: A sandstorm warning
senses.titleCN: 沙尘暴预警：气象服务
senses.definition: an official alert issued when a sandstorm is expected
senses.definitionCN: 预计出现沙尘暴时发布的官方警报
senses.example: Forecasters issued a sandstorm warning for the afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 预报员发布了下午的沙尘暴预警。
senses.why: forecasting turns the event into an alert, so the word names the official warning.
senses.whyCN: 预报把事件变成警报，因此这个词命名官方预警。

senses.title: The impacts of a sandstorm
senses.titleCN: 沙尘暴影响：能见度、交通与健康
senses.definition: the effects of a sandstorm on visibility, transport, health and equipment
senses.definitionCN: 沙尘暴对能见度、交通、健康与设备的影响
senses.example: Visibility fell to zero during the sandstorm.
senses.exampleCN: 沙尘暴期间能见度降为零。
senses.why: the event is also defined by its effects, so the word names impacts on visibility, transport and health.
senses.whyCN: 事件也由其影响界定，因此这个词命名对能见度、交通与健康的影响。

senses.title: An overwhelming surge
senses.titleCN: 比喻：铺天盖地、令人窒息的冲击
senses.definition: a sudden overwhelming quantity of something that feels like a storm of sand
senses.definitionCN: 突然铺天盖地、像沙暴一样令人窒息的量
senses.example: The office faced a sandstorm of complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室面对铺天盖地的投诉。
senses.why: the shape of a wall of sand is transferred to any overwhelming surge, giving the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 沙墙的形状被移到任何铺天盖地的冲击上，形成比喻。

intro.en: Sandstorm is a native English compound of sand and storm. Sand goes back to Old English sand, and storm to Old English storm. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sandstorm 是英语本族复合词，由 sand 与 storm 构成。sand 上承古英语 sand，storm 上承古英语 storm。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sand is the Germanic word for granular rock, with German Sand as a close relative.
items.cn: sand 是日耳曼语的颗粒岩石词，德语 Sand 是近亲。

items.en: Storm meant a tempest or violent weather; its deeper Germanic connections are reconstructed rather than certain.
items.cn: storm 指暴风雨或剧烈天气；其更早的日耳曼语联系属重构而非确定。

items.en: Sand plus storm appears in eighteenth- and nineteenth-century travel writing about deserts and dry plains.
items.cn: sand 加 storm 见于 18 与 19 世纪关于沙漠与干旱平原的游记。

items.en: Twentieth-century meteorology separates sandstorm from dust storm by particle size and height, and names regional types such as the haboob.
items.cn: 20 世纪气象学按颗粒大小与高度区分沙尘暴与尘暴，并命名哈布沙暴等区域类型。

items.en: Recent usage links sandstorms to desertification, air quality and respiratory health.
items.cn: 近期用法把沙尘暴与荒漠化、空气质量及呼吸健康联系起来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the parts are securely documented, but the compound's first citation is dated differently in different sources.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：两个成分均有可靠记载，但复合词的最早书证各家年代不一。

note.en: Group one holds the sand compounds most easily mistaken for sandstorm; group two holds the other wind-and-dust weather terms.
note.cn: 第一组是最易被误认成 sandstorm 的 sand 复合词；第二组是其他风沙天气术语。

entries.definition: Loose granular rock; a sandstorm is that material in violent motion.
entries.definitionCN: 松散的颗粒岩石；沙尘暴是它在剧烈运动中的状态。

entries.definition: Rock made of cemented sand grains; it is solid and has nothing to do with weather.
entries.definitionCN: 由胶结沙粒构成的岩石；它是固体，与天气无关。

entries.definition: Sand saturated with water that cannot support weight; it is still, not blown.
entries.definitionCN: 饱含水的沙，无法承重；它静止不动，不被风吹。

entries.definition: A ridge of sand built in water by currents or waves, not by a storm in the air.
entries.definitionCN: 水流或波浪在水中堆成的沙脊，不是空中风暴所造。

entries.definition: A storm carrying fine dust over a wider area, often higher in the air than a sandstorm.
entries.definitionCN: 携带细尘、范围更广的风暴，尘常被扬得比沙尘暴更高。

entries.definition: A violent sand or dust storm of the Sudan and Arabian regions, often forming a dense wall.
entries.definitionCN: 苏丹与阿拉伯地区的强沙尘暴，常形成致密沙墙。

entries.definition: A severe snowstorm with strong wind and low visibility; the same structure, a different load.
entries.definitionCN: 强风低能见度的暴雪；结构相同，负荷不同。

entries.definition: A hot, dusty wind from North Africa reaching the Mediterranean; the wind itself, not the storm.
entries.definitionCN: 从北非吹到地中海的干热多尘风；指风本身，而非风暴。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real neighbours, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与邻近术语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sand + storm: a storm whose cargo is sand.
normal.cn: sand + storm：货物是沙的风暴。

normal.en: Sandstorm is coarse and low; dust storm is fine and high.
normal.cn: 沙尘暴颗粒粗、位置低；尘暴颗粒细、扬得高。

normal.en: Blizzard is the same structure with snow; once you see the pattern, the words explain themselves.
normal.cn: blizzard 是同一结构换成雪；看懂模式，词就自我解释。

normal.en: A sandstorm warning is about visibility; a sandstorm source is about where the sand starts.
normal.cn: 沙尘暴预警关注能见度，沙源地关注沙从哪里起。

normal.en: Dry lake beds and deserts are the two classic sandstorm sources.
normal.cn: 干涸湖床与沙漠是两类典型的沙尘暴源地。

abstract.en: A sandstorm is a landscape that decides to travel.
abstract.cn: 沙尘暴是一块决定出行的景观。

abstract.en: A storm of complaints can bury a project as fast as any wall of sand.
abstract.cn: 投诉的风暴能像沙墙一样迅速埋掉一个项目。

abstract.en: The dust a sandstorm leaves is geography arriving at your window.
abstract.cn: 沙尘暴留下的尘土，是地理来到你的窗前。

examples.en: A sandstorm closed the airport for two days.
examples.cn: 沙尘暴使机场关闭了两天。

examples.en: Drivers were warned about the sandstorm on the highway.
examples.cn: 司机们收到高速公路上沙尘暴的警告。

examples.en: The sandstorm stripped the paint from the signs.
examples.cn: 沙尘暴剥掉了标牌上的漆。

dict_mnemonic.text: sand（沙）+ storm（风暴）＝以沙为负荷的风暴；与 dust storm（细尘）、blizzard（雪）、haboob（区域型）对照记忆。

root: 英语本族复合词，由 sand（沙，古英语 sand）与 storm（风暴，古英语 storm）组合。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of sandstorm. The weather event yields the sand it leaves, a countable occurrence, its source, its warning, its impacts, and finally any overwhelming surge.
sensesIntro.cn: sandstorm 的八个义项。天气事件衍生出落尘、可计数的一次事件、源地、预警、影响，最后是任何铺天盖地的冲击。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown wall of sand moves across the horizon and swallows the sun.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堵褐色沙墙越过地平线，把太阳吞掉。

branches.en: THE EVENT AND ITS LOAD: the storm as weather, then its coarse sand.
branches.cn: 事件与负荷：先是作为天气的风暴，再是其粗沙。

branches.en: WHAT IT LEAVES AND HOW OFTEN: deposited dust, then one countable occurrence.
branches.cn: 留下什么与发生几次：先是被落下的尘土，再是可计数的一次。

branches.en: WHERE IT BEGINS AND HOW IT IS ANNOUNCED: the source area, then the official warning.
branches.cn: 从何处起与如何预告：先是源地，再是官方预警。

branches.en: WHAT IT DOES: visibility, transport, health and equipment.
branches.cn: 它造成什么：能见度、交通、健康与设备。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any sudden overwhelming quantity.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何突然铺天盖地的量。

intro.en: Sandstorm is a bare compound of two free words. English adds only the plural -s; the interpretive work is done by the two nouns.
intro.cn: sandstorm 是两个自由词的直接复合。英语只加复数 -s；解释工作由两个名词完成。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic and have no Latin cognates. Latin arena means sand but is unrelated, and tempestas means storm but is likewise unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。拉丁 arena 意为沙、tempestas 意为风暴，但都与它不同源。

items.example: Sand filled the road.
The storm broke at noon.
A sandstorm hit the camp.
Spring brings frequent sandstorms.
items.exampleCN: 春天带来频繁的沙尘暴。

items.example: The soil is sandy and drains fast.
The crossing was stormy.
A dust storm reduced visibility across the plain.
items.exampleCN: 尘暴降低了平原上的能见度。

items.meaning: to clean or cut a surface with sand driven by air
items.meaningCN: 用气流喷沙清理或切割表面
items.example: They sandblasted the old paint away.
items.exampleCN: 他们用喷沙把旧漆打掉。

definition_zh: 肥沃的；能生育的；多产的；富于创造力的
definition_en: able to produce much growth, offspring or new ideas
core_image: 一把黑土在手里散开，土里全是根须和虫，种下去就冒芽
scene: 河滩上的黑土松软湿润，插下一根枝条，半个月后就长出新叶。The silt left by the flood made the riverbank fertile.
sceneCN: 这里 fertile 指「肥沃的、能长作物的」（第 1 个义项：土壤富含养分、适合植物生长）；句意为洪水留下的淤泥使河岸变得肥沃。

pos.zh: 肥沃的；能生育的；多产的；富于创造力的

derivatives.zh: fertil-（拉丁 fertilis「能承载的」）+ -ity（拉丁 -itas，表性质）→ 肥沃的性质：肥力、生育力
fertil-（拉丁 fertilis）+ -ize（希腊 -izein 经拉丁 -izare，表「使……化」）→ 使变得肥沃或受孕：施肥、使受精
fertilize + -er（古英语 -ere，施事后缀）→ 施行施肥之物：肥料
fertilize + -ation（拉丁 -atio，表动作或结果）→ 施肥或受精的行为：受精、施肥
in-（拉丁否定前缀）+ fertile（拉丁 fertilis）→ 不肥沃的；引申为不育的

senses.title: Soil rich enough to grow crops
senses.titleCN: 土壤肥沃：养分足、能长作物
senses.definition: soil that contains enough nutrients to support abundant plant growth
senses.definitionCN: 含有足够养分、能支撑植物旺盛生长的土壤
senses.example: The silt left by the flood made the riverbank fertile.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水留下的淤泥使河岸变得肥沃。
senses.why: fertile comes from ferre 'to bear', so fertile soil is soil that bears a great deal.
senses.whyCN: fertile 来自 ferre「承载、产出」，因此肥沃的土壤就是能产出很多的土壤。

senses.title: Land that produces plenty
senses.titleCN: 土地富饶：物产丰足的地区
senses.definition: land that yields abundant crops or resources
senses.definitionCN: 出产大量作物或资源的土地
senses.example: The river valley is the most fertile land in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河谷是该地区最富饶的土地。
senses.why: productivity is a property of land, not only of soil, so the adjective extends from the sample to the region.
senses.whyCN: 生产力是土地的性质，而不只是土壤的性质，因此形容词从样本扩展到地区。

senses.title: Able to produce offspring
senses.titleCN: 能生育的：有繁殖能力的
senses.definition: capable of reproducing, of an animal or a person
senses.definitionCN: 能繁殖的，用于动物或人
senses.example: The queen is fertile only in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 蜂后只在春天有繁殖力。
senses.why: the same capacity to bear applies to animals, so the adjective moves from crops to offspring.
senses.whyCN: 同样的承载能力适用于动物，因此形容词从作物转到后代。

senses.title: Capable of developing, as an egg or spore
senses.titleCN: 可育的：卵、孢子、花粉能发育
senses.definition: able to develop into a new organism, as a fertilised egg or a viable spore
senses.definitionCN: 能发育为新个体的，如受精卵或可育孢子
senses.example: Only fertile spores germinate on the damp rock.
senses.exampleCN: 只有可育孢子在潮湿岩石上发芽。
senses.why: an egg or spore is fertile when it can develop, which is the biological narrowing of the same idea.
senses.whyCN: 卵或孢子能发育时便是可育的，这是同一观念在生物学上的收窄。

senses.title: An imagination that produces much
senses.titleCN: 富于创造力：能不断产生想法
senses.definition: producing many ideas or images; inventive
senses.definitionCN: 能产生许多想法或意象的；有创造力的
senses.example: She has a fertile imagination and writes a story a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她想象力丰富，每周写一个故事。
senses.why: a mind that bears many ideas repeats the agricultural image, with thoughts as the crop.
senses.whyCN: 能承载许多观念的心智重复了农业意象，以思想为作物。

senses.title: Ground that encourages something
senses.titleCN: 温床：易于滋生某事物的环境
senses.definition: a situation or place that allows something, often unwanted, to develop
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物（常为不受欢迎者）得以发展的环境
senses.example: Rumour finds fertile ground in a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言在小镇上容易找到滋生的土壤。
senses.why: the agricultural image is transferred: an idea or rumour is treated as a crop that the ground will grow.
senses.whyCN: 农业意象被移用：想法或谣言被当作土地会种出的作物。

senses.title: Capable of being converted, in nuclear physics
senses.titleCN: 核物理：可转换的（增殖性材料）
senses.definition: of a material that can be converted into fissile fuel in a reactor
senses.definitionCN: 可在反应堆中转化为裂变燃料的材料
senses.example: Fertile isotopes are converted into fissile ones inside the reactor.
senses.exampleCN: 增殖性同位素在反应堆内被转化为裂变性同位素。
senses.why: physics borrows the biological sense: the material is fertile because it can be transformed into something that yields energy.
senses.whyCN: 物理学借用生物义：材料之所以「可育」，因为它能转化为释放能量之物。

senses.title: Well supplied with nutrients
senses.titleCN: 农业义：肥力充足的
senses.definition: having had nutrients added or restored, as a field after fertilising
senses.definitionCN: 已添加或恢复养分，如施肥后的田地
senses.example: The fertile field yielded two harvests that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那块肥力充足的田当年收了两季。
senses.why: a field is fertile after nutrients are restored, which is the agricultural sense narrowed to managed land.
senses.whyCN: 田地在养分恢复后肥沃，这是农业义收窄到受管理的土地。

intro.en: Fertile comes from Latin fertilis 'fruitful', from ferre 'to bear, carry', and reached English through Old French in the fifteenth century. The Latin verb also underlies infer, transfer and refer. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fertile 来自拉丁 fertilis「多产的」，出 ferre「承载、携带」，15 世纪经古法语进入英语。这个拉丁动词也是 infer、transfer、refer 的词基。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ferre meant to bear, carry or bring, and became one of the most productive verbs in Latin, appearing in infer, transfer, refer, offer and prefer.
items.cn: ferre 意为承载、携带、带来，是拉丁语中构词力最强的动词之一，见于 infer、transfer、refer、offer、prefer。

items.en: Fertilis 'fruitful, abundant' was formed from ferre with the suffix -ilis 'able to', so the adjective means able to bear.
items.cn: fertilis「多产的、丰盛的」由 ferre 加后缀 -ilis「能够」构成，因此形容词意为「能承载产出的」。

items.en: Old French fertile passed into English in the fifteenth century, first of land and soil.
items.cn: 古法语 fertile 在 15 世纪进入英语，最初用于土地与土壤。

items.en: Seventeenth- and eighteenth-century agricultural writing fixes fertile soil and fertile land as standard collocations.
items.cn: 17 与 18 世纪的农业文献把 fertile soil 与 fertile land 固定为标准搭配。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology extends fertile to eggs, spores and organisms able to reproduce.
items.cn: 19 世纪生物学把 fertile 扩展到能繁殖的卵、孢子与生物体。

items.en: Source uncertain: the Indo-European root behind ferre is widely reconstructed as a 'to carry' root, but its exact semantic range is debated; first dates above are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：ferre 背后的印欧词根常被重构为「携带」义，但其确切语义范围仍有争论；上述首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words that are not from ferre; group two holds the synonyms of productive growth.
note.cn: 第一组是形近但不来自 ferre 的词；第二组是「多产、丰盛」的近义词。

entries.definition: Producing no useful result; it comes from Latin futilis 'easily poured out', not from ferre.
entries.definitionCN: 不产生有用结果；来自拉丁 futilis「容易倒出」，并非 ferre。

entries.definition: Containing iron; from Latin ferrum 'iron', which is unrelated to ferre.
entries.definitionCN: 含铁的；来自拉丁 ferrum「铁」，与 ferre 无关。

entries.definition: Wild or untamed, from Latin fera 'wild animal'; it only looks like fertile.
entries.definitionCN: 野生的、未驯化的，来自拉丁 fera「野兽」；只是形似 fertile。
